modules.title: Continuous linear maps
modules.doc:
This file collects auxiliary results about `ContinuousLinearMap`s that are not (yet) available in
Mathlib.

## Main results

* `ContinuousLinearMap.ker_mk`: the kernel of the continuous linear map built from a continuous
  semilinear map `f` agrees with the kernel of `f`.
* `ContinuousLinearMap.support_eq_sup_eigenspace_nonzero`: the range of a symmetric continuous
  linear map on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space is the supremum of its eigenspaces for
  nonzero eigenvalues.

    (ContinuousLinearMap.mk f hf).ker = LinearMap.ker f

modules.title: Products of functions on a finite product
modules.doc:
With at least one coordinate, a function `T` on a finite product `(i : ι) → κ i` is a product of
functions of one variable exactly when it satisfies the exchange relations.

## i. Overview

For a function `T : ((i : ι) → κ i) → K` with values in a field, the exchange relations say
that for every coordinate `i`, values `a b : κ i` and points `x y`,
`T (x[i ← a]) * T (y[i ← b]) = T (x[i ← b]) * T (y[i ← a])`, where `x[i ← a]` is `x` with
coordinate `i` replaced by `a`. They say that all `2 × 2` minors of the one-coordinate
flattenings of `T` vanish. The flattening at `i` has rows indexed by `κ i` and columns indexed
by assignments to the remaining coordinates.

If the index type `ι` is finite and nonempty, the exchange relations hold exactly when
`T x = ∏ i, v i (x i)` for some functions `v i : κ i → K`. Nonemptiness is necessary: if `ι` is
empty, the exchange relations are vacuous, so every function satisfies them, but an empty
product is always `1`.

For finite-dimensional tensors, these equations characterize the tensors of rank at most one,
which form the affine cone over the Segre variety.

This file is a temporary copy of results intended for Mathlib.

## ii. Key results

- `exists_prod_iff_mul_update` : with at least one coordinate, `T` is a product of functions of
  one variable if and only if it satisfies the exchange relations.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Product identities
- B. Factorization from the exchange relations

## iv. References

- M. Michałek and B. Sturmfels, Invitation to Nonlinear Algebra, §9.2, p. 141.
  [ref: michalek_sturmfels_2021]

sections.text: ## A. Product identities
## B. Factorization from the exchange relations

declarations.name: Finset.prod_apply_update
declarations.doc:
Changing coordinate `i` of `x` to `a` changes only the factor indexed by `i` in
`∏ j, v j (x j)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma Finset.prod_apply_update (v : (i : ι) → κ i → K) (x : (i : ι) → κ i) (i : ι)
    (a : κ i) : ∏ j, v j (update x i a j) = v i a * ∏ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, v j (x j)

declarations.name: Finset.prod_update_const_mul
declarations.doc: Multiplying the function indexed by `i₀` by `c` multiplies `∏ i, v i (x i)` by `c`.
declarations.statement:
lemma Finset.prod_update_const_mul (v : (i : ι) → κ i → K) (c : K) (i₀ : ι)
    (x : (i : ι) → κ i) :
    ∏ i, update v i₀ (fun a ↦ c * v i₀ a) i (x i) = c * ∏ i, v i (x i)

declarations.name: prod_apply_update_mul_prod_apply_update
declarations.doc:
A product `x ↦ ∏ i, v i (x i)` of functions of one variable satisfies the exchange
relations.
declarations.statement:
lemma prod_apply_update_mul_prod_apply_update (v : (i : ι) → κ i → K) (x y : (i : ι) → κ i)
    (i : ι) (a b : κ i) :
    (∏ j, v j (update x i a j)) * ∏ j, v j (update y i b j) =
      (∏ j, v j (update x i b j)) * ∏ j, v j (update y i a j)

declarations.name: eq_mul_prod_of_mul_update
declarations.doc:
If `T` satisfies the exchange relations and `T x₀ ≠ 0`, then every `x` that agrees with `x₀`
outside a finite set `s` of coordinates satisfies
`T x = T x₀ * ∏ j ∈ s, T (update x₀ j (x j)) / T x₀`.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_mul_prod_of_mul_update {T : ((i : ι) → κ i) → K}
    (hT : ∀ i (a b : κ i) x y, T (update x i a) * T (update y i b) =
      T (update x i b) * T (update y i a))
    {x₀ : (i : ι) → κ i} (h₀ : T x₀ ≠ 0) (s : Finset ι) :
    ∀ x : (i : ι) → κ i, (∀ j ∉ s, x j = x₀ j) →
      T x = T x₀ * ∏ j ∈ s, T (update x₀ j (x j)) / T x₀

declarations.name: exists_prod_of_mul_update
declarations.doc:
If `ι` is nonempty, a function on a finite product that satisfies the exchange relations
factors as a product of functions of one variable.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_prod_of_mul_update [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] {T : ((i : ι) → κ i) → K}
    (hT : ∀ i (a b : κ i) x y, T (update x i a) * T (update y i b) =
      T (update x i b) * T (update y i a)) :
    ∃ v : (i : ι) → κ i → K, ∀ x, T x = ∏ i, v i (x i)

declarations.name: exists_prod_iff_mul_update
declarations.doc:
If `ι` is nonempty, a function on a finite product factors as a product of functions of one
variable if and only if it satisfies the exchange relations.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_prod_iff_mul_update [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] {T : ((i : ι) → κ i) → K} :
    (∃ v : (i : ι) → κ i → K, ∀ x, T x = ∏ i, v i (x i)) ↔
      ∀ i (a b : κ i) x y, T (update x i a) * T (update y i b) =
        T (update x i b) * T (update y i a)

modules.title: `2 × 2` block operators on a Hilbert sum
modules.doc:
This file develops the operator-matrix ("block operator") calculus on the two-fold Hilbert
sum `ℋ ⊕ ℋ`, the main tool in the block-operator proof of the Jensen operator inequality.

## Main definitions

* `HSum ℋ`: the `ℓ²` direct sum `ℋ ⊕ ℋ` of two copies of a Hilbert space `ℋ`, realised as
  `PiLp 2 (fun _ : Fin 2 => ℋ)`.
* `hsumProj`, `hsumIncl`: the coordinate projections `HSum ℋ →L[ℂ] ℋ` and inclusions
  `ℋ →L[ℂ] HSum ℋ` exhibiting `HSum ℋ` as a direct sum; they are mutually adjoint.
* `blockDiagonal A B`: the block-diagonal operator `diag(A, B)` on `HSum ℋ`.
* `blockOp A00 A01 A10 A11`: a general `2 × 2` block operator on `HSum ℋ`.
* `blockDiagonalHom`: the `⋆`-algebra homomorphism `(A, B) ↦ diag(A, B)`.

Here `L ℋ = ℋ →L[ℂ] ℋ` is the algebra of bounded operators (quantum observables) on `ℋ`;
representing a pair of observables as a block-diagonal operator on `ℋ ⊕ ℋ` is the dilation
trick underlying the operator inequalities used throughout quantum information theory.

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.HSum
declarations.doc:
A two-fold Hilbert sum used for the block-operator proof of Jensen's inequality.
The inner-product instance on `ℋ` is unused by the underlying type synonym but kept to
document that `HSum ℋ` is the `ℓ²` direct sum of two copies of a Hilbert space.
declarations.statement: abbrev HSum (ℋ : Type u) [NormedAddCommGroup ℋ] [InnerProductSpace ℂ ℋ] : Type u

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.hsumEquiv
declarations.doc:
The continuous linear equivalence between the Hilbert sum `HSum ℋ` and the plain
function space `Fin 2 → ℋ`, forgetting the `ℓ²` inner-product structure on the index.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def hsumEquiv (ℋ : Type u) [NormedAddCommGroup ℋ] [InnerProductSpace ℂ ℋ] :
    HSum ℋ ≃L[ℂ] (Fin 2 → ℋ)

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.hsumProj
declarations.doc:
The `i`-th coordinate projection `HSum ℋ →L[ℂ] ℋ` of the Hilbert sum onto its
`i`-th summand.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def hsumProj (ℋ : Type u) [NormedAddCommGroup ℋ] [InnerProductSpace ℂ ℋ]
    (i : Fin 2) : HSum ℋ →L[ℂ] ℋ

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.hsumIncl
declarations.doc:
The `i`-th coordinate inclusion `ℋ →L[ℂ] HSum ℋ`, embedding `ℋ` as the `i`-th summand
of the Hilbert sum and placing `0` in the other summand.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def hsumIncl (ℋ : Type u) [NormedAddCommGroup ℋ] [InnerProductSpace ℂ ℋ]
    (i : Fin 2) : ℋ →L[ℂ] HSum ℋ

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.hsumProj_hsumIncl_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma hsumProj_hsumIncl_apply (i j : Fin 2) (x : ℋ) :
    hsumProj ℋ i (hsumIncl ℋ j x) = if i = j then x else 0

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.inner_hsumIncl_hsumIncl
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_hsumIncl_hsumIncl (i j : Fin 2) (x y : ℋ) :
    inner ℂ (hsumIncl ℋ i x) (hsumIncl ℋ j y) = if i = j then inner ℂ x y else 0

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.hsumIncl_adjoint
declarations.statement:
lemma hsumIncl_adjoint (i : Fin 2) :
    (hsumIncl ℋ i).adjoint = hsumProj ℋ i

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.hsumProj_adjoint
declarations.statement:
lemma hsumProj_adjoint (i : Fin 2) :
    (hsumProj ℋ i).adjoint = hsumIncl ℋ i

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.hsumIncl_proj_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma hsumIncl_proj_sum (z : HSum ℋ) :
    hsumIncl ℋ 0 (hsumProj ℋ 0 z) + hsumIncl ℋ 1 (hsumProj ℋ 1 z) = z

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.blockDiagonal
declarations.doc: The block diagonal operator `diag(A, B)` on the two-fold Hilbert sum.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def blockDiagonal (A B : L ℋ) : L (HSum ℋ)

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.blockOp
declarations.doc: A general `2 × 2` block operator on `HSum ℋ`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def blockOp (A00 A01 A10 A11 : L ℋ) : L (HSum ℋ)

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.blockOp_ext
declarations.statement:
lemma blockOp_ext {T S : L (HSum ℋ)}
    (h0 : ∀ z : HSum ℋ, hsumProj ℋ 0 (T z) = hsumProj ℋ 0 (S z))
    (h1 : ∀ z : HSum ℋ, hsumProj ℋ 1 (T z) = hsumProj ℋ 1 (S z)) :
    T = S

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.blockDiagonal_star
declarations.statement:
lemma blockDiagonal_star (A B : L ℋ) :
    star (blockDiagonal (ℋ := ℋ) A B) = blockDiagonal (ℋ := ℋ) (star A) (star B)

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.blockDiagonalHom
declarations.doc:
The `ℝ`-`⋆`-algebra homomorphism sending a pair of operators `(A, B)` to the
block-diagonal operator `diag(A, B)` on the Hilbert sum.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def blockDiagonalHom : (L ℋ × L ℋ) →⋆ₐ[ℝ] L (HSum ℋ)

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.blockDiagonalHom_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma blockDiagonalHom_apply (p : L ℋ × L ℋ) :
    blockDiagonalHom (ℋ := ℋ) p = blockDiagonal (ℋ := ℋ) p.1 p.2

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.hsumProj_blockDiagonal_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma hsumProj_blockDiagonal_zero (A B : L ℋ) (z : HSum ℋ) :
    hsumProj ℋ 0 (blockDiagonal A B z) = A (hsumProj ℋ 0 z)

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.hsumProj_blockDiagonal_one
declarations.statement:
lemma hsumProj_blockDiagonal_one (A B : L ℋ) (z : HSum ℋ) :
    hsumProj ℋ 1 (blockDiagonal A B z) = B (hsumProj ℋ 1 z)

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.blockDiagonal_one
declarations.statement:
lemma blockDiagonal_one :
    blockDiagonal (ℋ := ℋ) (1 : L ℋ) (1 : L ℋ) = (1 : L (HSum ℋ))

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.blockDiagonal_nonneg
declarations.statement:
lemma blockDiagonal_nonneg {A B : L ℋ} (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hB : 0 ≤ B) :
    0 ≤ blockDiagonal (ℋ := ℋ) A B

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.hsumProj_blockOp_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma hsumProj_blockOp_zero (A00 A01 A10 A11 : L ℋ) (z : HSum ℋ) :
    hsumProj ℋ 0 (blockOp (ℋ := ℋ) A00 A01 A10 A11 z) =
      A00 (hsumProj ℋ 0 z) + A01 (hsumProj ℋ 1 z)

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.hsumProj_blockOp_one
declarations.statement:
lemma hsumProj_blockOp_one (A00 A01 A10 A11 : L ℋ) (z : HSum ℋ) :
    hsumProj ℋ 1 (blockOp (ℋ := ℋ) A00 A01 A10 A11 z) =
      A10 (hsumProj ℋ 0 z) + A11 (hsumProj ℋ 1 z)

declarations.name: JensenOperatorInequality.blockOp_star
declarations.statement:
lemma blockOp_star (A00 A01 A10 A11 : L ℋ) :
    star (blockOp (ℋ := ℋ) A00 A01 A10 A11) =
      blockOp (ℋ := ℋ) (star A00) (star A10) (star A01) (star A11)

## 構造（Core / Wrapper）

このファイルは Löwner–Heinz まわりの議論を、**一般の C★代数 `𝓐`** 上で再利用できるように
Core として切り出したものです。

- `section Pure`：`cfcR` と `OperatorMonotone(On)` / `OperatorConvexOn` などの **定義**（軽い層）
- `section Spectrum`：`NonnegSpectrumClass` などを仮定して、主要定理群を置く **重い層**
- `namespace LownerHeinzCore.Spectral`：`spectralOrder` を **`local instance`** として閉じ込めた wrapper

`spectralOrder` を Core 本体に混ぜず、wrapper 側で局所化することで、他モジュールへの順序変更が
漏れないようにしています。また `NonnegSpectrumClass` は必要な層で明示し、場当たりの `infer_instance`
散布を避けています。

declarations.name: HermitianMat.conj
declarations.doc:
The Hermitian matrix given by conjugating by a (possibly rectangular) Matrix. If we required `B` to be
square, this would apply to any `Semigroup`+`StarMul` (as proved by `IsSelfAdjoint.conjugate`). But this lets
us conjugate to other sizes too, as is done in e.g. Kraus operators. That is, it's a _heterogeneous_ conjguation.
declarations.statement: def conj {m} (B : Matrix m n α) : HermitianMat n α →+ HermitianMat m α

declarations.name: HermitianMat.conj_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma conj_apply (B : Matrix m n α) (A : HermitianMat n α) :
    conj B A = ⟨B * A.mat * B.conjTranspose, (conj B A).2⟩

declarations.name: HermitianMat.conj_apply_mat
declarations.statement:
lemma conj_apply_mat (B : Matrix m n α) (A : HermitianMat n α) :
    (A.conj B).mat = B * A.mat * B.conjTranspose

declarations.name: HermitianMat.conj_conj
declarations.statement:
lemma conj_conj {m l} [Fintype m] (B : Matrix m n α) (C : Matrix l m α) :
    (A.conj B).conj C = A.conj (C * B)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.conj_zero
declarations.statement: lemma conj_zero [DecidableEq n] : A.conj (0 : Matrix m n α) = 0

declarations.name: HermitianMat.conj_one

declarations.name: HermitianMat.conj_one_unitary
declarations.statement:
lemma conj_one_unitary [DecidableEq n] (U : Matrix.unitaryGroup n α) :
    conj U.val 1 = 1

declarations.name: HermitianMat.conjLinear_apply
declarations.statement: lemma conjLinear_apply (B : Matrix m n α) : conjLinear R B A = conj B A

declarations.statement:
lemma kronecker_diagonal [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (d₁ : m → ℝ) (d₂ : n → ℝ) :

declarations.name: HermitianMat.kron_commute
declarations.doc: A ⊗ₖ B always commutes with C ⊗ₖ D if the pairs commute.
declarations.statement:
theorem kron_commute [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n]
    {A C : HermitianMat m α} {B D : HermitianMat n α}
    (hAC : Commute A.mat C.mat) (hBD : Commute B.mat D.mat):
    Commute (A ⊗ₖ B).mat (C ⊗ₖ D).mat

theorem kron_id_commute_id_kro [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n]
    (A : HermitianMat m α) (B : HermitianMat n α) :
    Commute (A ⊗ₖ (1 : HermitianMat n α)).mat ((1 : HermitianMat m α) ⊗ₖ B).mat

declarations.statement:
lemma kronecker_conj [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

    (A ⊗ₖ B).conj (C ⊗ₖ D) = (A.conj C) ⊗ₖ (B.conj D)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.spectrum_rcLike
declarations.doc:
We fix a simp-normal form that, for HermitianMat, we always work in terms
of the real spectrum.

theorem spectrum_rcLike (A : HermitianMat n 𝕜) :

modules.doc: Matrix operations on HermitianMats with the CFC

sections.text:
Here we give HermitianMat versions of many cfc theorems, like `cfc_id`, `cfc_sub`, `cfc_comp`,
etc. We need these because (as above) `HermitianMat.cfc` is different from `_root_.cfc`.

declarations.statement: lemma isSelfAdjoint : IsSelfAdjoint A.mat

lemma continuousOn_finite {α β : Type*} (f : α → β) (S : Set α)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.conjTranspose_cfc
declarations.statement: lemma conjTranspose_cfc : (cfc f A.mat).conjTranspose = cfc f A.mat

lemma cfc_eq_cfc_iff_eqOn (f g : ℝ → ℝ) :

lemma cfc_commute (f g : ℝ → ℝ) (hAB : Commute A.mat B.mat) :

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_reindex
declarations.doc: Reindexing a matrix commutes with applying the CFC.
declarations.statement: theorem cfc_reindex (e : d ≃ d₂) : (A.reindex e).cfc f = (A.cfc f).reindex e

declarations.name: HermitianMat.spectrum_cfc_eq_image
declarations.statement:
lemma spectrum_cfc_eq_image (A : HermitianMat d 𝕜) (f : ℝ → ℝ) :
    spectrum ℝ (A.cfc f).mat = f '' (spectrum ℝ A.mat)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_toMat_eq_sum_smul_proj
declarations.doc: Spectral decomposition of `A.cfc f` as a sum of scaled projections (matrix version).
declarations.statement:
theorem cfc_toMat_eq_sum_smul_proj : (A.cfc f).mat =
    ∑ i, f (A.H.eigenvalues i) • (A.H.eigenvectorUnitary.val * (Matrix.single i i 1) * A.H.eigenvectorUnitary.val.conjTranspose)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_eigenvalues
declarations.statement:
lemma cfc_eigenvalues (A : HermitianMat d 𝕜) :

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_id
declarations.statement: nonrec lemma cfc_id : A.cfc id = A

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_id'
declarations.statement: nonrec lemma cfc_id' : A.cfc (·) = A

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_add
declarations.statement: nonrec lemma cfc_add : A.cfc (f + g) = A.cfc f + A.cfc g

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_add_apply
declarations.statement: lemma cfc_add_apply : A.cfc (fun x ↦ f x + g x) = A.cfc f + A.cfc g

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_sub
declarations.statement: nonrec lemma cfc_sub : A.cfc (f - g) = A.cfc f - A.cfc g

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_sub_apply
declarations.statement: lemma cfc_sub_apply : A.cfc (fun x ↦ f x - g x) = A.cfc f - A.cfc g

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_neg
declarations.statement: nonrec lemma cfc_neg : A.cfc (-f) = -A.cfc f

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_neg_apply
declarations.statement: lemma cfc_neg_apply : A.cfc (fun x ↦ -f x) = -A.cfc f

declarations.name: HermitianMat.mat_cfc_mul
declarations.doc:
We don't have a direct analog of `cfc_mul`, since we can't generally multiply
to HermitianMat's to get another one, so the theorem statement wouldn't be well-typed.
But, we can say that the matrices are always equal. See `cfc_conj` for the coe-free
analog to multiplication.
declarations.statement: theorem mat_cfc_mul : (A.cfc (f * g)).mat = A.cfc f * A.cfc g

declarations.name: HermitianMat.mat_cfc_mul_apply
declarations.statement: lemma mat_cfc_mul_apply : (A.cfc (fun x ↦ f x * g x)).mat = A.cfc f * A.cfc g

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_comp
declarations.statement: nonrec lemma cfc_comp : A.cfc (g ∘ f) = (A.cfc f).cfc g

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_comp_apply
declarations.statement: lemma cfc_comp_apply : A.cfc (fun x ↦ g (f x)) = (A.cfc f).cfc g

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_conj
declarations.statement: nonrec lemma cfc_conj : (A.cfc f).conj (A.cfc g) = A.cfc (f * g^2)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_diagonal
declarations.statement: lemma cfc_diagonal (g : d → ℝ) : (diagonal 𝕜 g).cfc f = diagonal 𝕜 (f ∘ g)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_conj_unitary
declarations.statement:
lemma cfc_conj_unitary (U : Matrix.unitaryGroup d 𝕜) :
    (A.conj U.val).cfc f = (A.cfc f).conj U

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_const
declarations.statement: nonrec lemma cfc_const : (A.cfc (fun _ ↦ r)) = r • 1

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_const_mul_id
declarations.statement: nonrec lemma cfc_const_mul_id : A.cfc (fun x ↦ r * x) = r • A

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_const_mul
declarations.statement: nonrec lemma cfc_const_mul : A.cfc (fun x ↦ r * f x) = r • A.cfc f

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_apply_zero
declarations.statement: nonrec lemma cfc_apply_zero : (0 : HermitianMat d 𝕜).cfc f = f 0 • 1

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_apply_one
declarations.statement: nonrec lemma cfc_apply_one : (1 : HermitianMat d 𝕜).cfc f = f 1 • 1

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_pow
declarations.statement: lemma cfc_pow {n : ℕ} : A.cfc (· ^ n) = A ^ n

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_nonneg_iff
declarations.statement: lemma cfc_nonneg_iff : 0 ≤ A.cfc f ↔ ∀ i, 0 ≤ f (A.H.eigenvalues i)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_posDef
declarations.statement: lemma cfc_posDef : (A.cfc f).mat.PosDef ↔ ∀ i, 0 < f (A.H.eigenvalues i)

declarations.doc: If a rael function preserves nonnegativity, the CFC preserves PSDness.
declarations.statement:
theorem cfc_nonneg_of_nonneg (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hf : ∀ i ≥ 0, 0 ≤ f i) :
    0 ≤ A.cfc f

declarations.statement:
lemma trace_mul_cfc (A : HermitianMat d 𝕜) (f : ℝ → ℝ) :

declarations.statement:
lemma norm_eq_sum_eigenvalues_sq (A : HermitianMat d 𝕜) :

declarations.statement: lemma ball_subset_Icc : Metric.ball A r ⊆ Set.Icc (A - r • 1) (A + r • 1)

theorem continuous_cfc_fun {f : X → ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ∀ i, Continuous (f · i)) :

declarations.doc: Bound the Frobenius norm of a functional calculus application.

declarations.statement:
lemma norm_cfc_sub_cfc_le_sqrt_card {A : HermitianMat d ℂ} {f g : ℝ → ℝ} :
    ‖A.cfc f - A.cfc g‖ ≤ Real.sqrt (Fintype.card d) * ⨆ x ∈ spectrum ℝ A.mat, ‖f x - g x‖

HermitianMat.dist_lt_of_continuous'
declarations.doc: If $f$ is jointly continuous on $S \times T$ and $T$ is compact, then $x \mapsto f(x, \cdot)$ is continuous into the space of bounded functions on $T$ with the uniform norm.
declarations.statement:
lemma dist_lt_of_continuous' {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
    {f : X → ℝ → ℝ} {S : Set X} {T : Set ℝ}
    (hT : IsCompact T)
    (hf : ContinuousOn (fun (p : X × ℝ) ↦ f p.1 p.2) (S ×ˢ T))
    {x₀ : X} (hx₀ : x₀ ∈ S) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ U ∈ nhds x₀, ∀ x ∈ U ∩ S, ∀ t ∈ T, ‖f x t - f x₀ t‖ < ε

declarations.name: HermitianMat.continuousOn_cfc_of_compact
declarations.doc: The functional calculus is continuous on matrices with spectrum in a compact set.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuousOn_cfc_of_compact {K : Set ℝ} {g : ℝ → ℝ} (hK : IsCompact K) (hg : ContinuousOn g K) :
    ContinuousOn (fun (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) ↦ A.cfc g) {A | spectrum ℝ A.mat ⊆ K}

declarations.name: HermitianMat.continuous_cfc_joint_compact
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_cfc_joint_compact {X d : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
  {f : X → ℝ → ℝ} {A : X → HermitianMat d ℂ} {S : Set X} {T : Set ℝ}
  (hT : IsCompact T)
  (hf : ContinuousOn (fun (p : X × ℝ) ↦ f p.1 p.2) (S ×ˢ T))
  (hA₁ : ∀ x ∈ S, spectrum ℝ (A x).mat ⊆ T)
  (hA₂ : ContinuousOn (fun x ↦ A x) S) :
    ContinuousOn (fun x ↦ (A x).cfc (f x)) S

declarations.statement:
lemma eigenvalue_norm_le (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (i : d) :
    |A.H.eigenvalues i| ≤ ‖A‖

declarations.doc: The spectrum of a `HermitianMat` is contained in the closed ball of radius `‖A‖` around 0.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectrum_subset_closedBall (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) :

HermitianMat.dist_lt_of_continuous_spectrum
declarations.statement:
lemma dist_lt_of_continuous_spectrum {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
    {f : X → ℝ → ℝ} {A : X → HermitianMat d ℂ} {S : Set X} {T : Set ℝ}
    (hf : ContinuousOn (fun (p : X × ℝ) ↦ f p.1 p.2) (S ×ˢ T))
    (hA₁ : ∀ x ∈ S, spectrum ℝ (A x).mat ⊆ T)
    (hA₂ : ContinuousOn (fun x ↦ A x) S)
    {x₀ : X} (hx₀ : x₀ ∈ S) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :

declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_cfc_joint {X d : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]

declarations.doc: Specialization of `continuousOn_cfc_fun` for nonsingular matrices.

declarations.name: HermitianMat.inv_cfc_eq_cfc_inv
declarations.doc: The inverse of the CFC is the CFC of the inverse function.
declarations.statement:
lemma inv_cfc_eq_cfc_inv (hf : ∀ i, f (A.H.eigenvalues i) ≠ 0) :
    (A.cfc f)⁻¹ = A.cfc (fun u ↦ (f u)⁻¹)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_inv
declarations.statement: lemma cfc_inv [NonSingular A] : A.cfc (fun u ↦ u⁻¹) = A⁻¹

declarations.name: HermitianMat.integral_toMat
declarations.doc: The integral of a Hermitian matrix function commutes with `toMat`.

declarations.name: HermitianMat.intervalIntegrable_sum_smul_const
declarations.doc: A sum of scaled constant matrices is integrable if the scalar functions are integrable.
declarations.statement:
lemma intervalIntegrable_sum_smul_const (T₁ T₂ : ℝ) {μ : Measure ℝ} (g : ℝ → d → ℝ)
    (P : d → Matrix d d 𝕜) (hg : ∀ i, IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ g t i) μ T₁ T₂) :
    IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ ∑ i, g t i • P i) μ T₁ T₂

declarations.name: HermitianMat.intervalIntegrable_toMat_iff
declarations.doc: A function to Hermitian matrices is integrable iff its matrix values are integrable.
declarations.statement:
lemma intervalIntegrable_toMat_iff (A : ℝ → HermitianMat d 𝕜) (T₁ T₂ : ℝ) {μ : Measure ℝ} :
    IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ (A t).mat) μ T₁ T₂ ↔ IntervalIntegrable A μ T₁ T₂

declarations.name: HermitianMat.integrable_cfc
declarations.doc: The CFC of an integrable function family is integrable.

declarations.name: HermitianMat.integral_cfc_eq_cfc_integral
declarations.doc: The integral of the CFC is the CFC of the integral.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_cfc_eq_cfc_integral (T₁ T₂ : ℝ) {μ : Measure ℝ} (f : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ i, IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ f t (A.H.eigenvalues i)) μ T₁ T₂) :
    ∫ t in T₁..T₂, A.cfc (f t) ∂μ = A.cfc (fun u ↦ ∫ t in T₁..T₂, f t u ∂μ)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_pos_of_pos
declarations.statement:
lemma cfc_pos_of_pos {A : HermitianMat d 𝕜} {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hA : 0 < A)
    (hf : ∀ i > 0, 0 < f i) (hf₂ : 0 ≤ f 0) : 0 < A.cfc f

declarations.name: Commute.exists_HermitianMat_cfc
declarations.doc:
If two matrices A and B commute, then they is a common matrix with which they are both CFCs of.
This is a variant of the common theorem that "commuting matrices can be simultaneously diagonalized."
declarations.statement:
theorem _root_.Commute.exists_HermitianMat_cfc (hAB : Commute A.mat B.mat) :
    ∃ C : HermitianMat d 𝕜, (∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, A = C.cfc f) ∧ (∃ g : ℝ → ℝ, B = C.cfc g)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_le_cfc_of_PosDef
declarations.statement:
lemma cfc_le_cfc_of_PosDef (hfg : ∀ i, 0 < i → f i ≤ g i) (hA : A.mat.PosDef) :
    A.cfc f ≤ A.cfc g

lemma cfc_le_cfc_of_commute_monoOn (hf : MonotoneOn f (Set.Ioi 0))
  (hAB₁ : Commute A.mat B.mat) (hAB₂ : A ≤ B) (hA : A.mat.PosDef) (hB : B.mat.PosDef) :
    A.cfc f ≤ B.cfc f

declarations.doc: TODO: See above
declarations.statement:
theorem cfc_le_cfc_of_commute (hf : Monotone f) (hAB₁ : Commute A.mat B.mat) (hAB₂ : A ≤ B) :

HermitianMat.inv_ge_one_of_le_one
declarations.statement: lemma inv_ge_one_of_le_one (hA : A.mat.PosDef) (h : A ≤ 1) : 1 ≤ A⁻¹

declarations.name: HermitianMat.trace_cfc_eq
declarations.doc: The trace of cfc(f, A) equals the sum of f applied to eigenvalues.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_cfc_eq (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) :
    (A.cfc f).trace = ∑ i, f (A.H.eigenvalues i)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.mulVec_eq_zero_iff_inner_eigenvector_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma mulVec_eq_zero_iff_inner_eigenvector_zero
    (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ d) :
    A.mat.mulVec x = 0 ↔ ∀ i, A.H.eigenvalues i ≠ 0 → inner ℂ (A.H.eigenvectorBasis i) x = 0

declarations.name: HermitianMat.cfc_mulVec_expansion
declarations.statement:
lemma cfc_mulVec_expansion (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (x : EuclideanSpace ℂ d) :
    (A.cfc f).mat.mulVec x = ∑ i, (f (A.H.eigenvalues i) : ℂ) • inner ℂ (A.H.eigenvectorBasis i) x • A.H.eigenvectorBasis i

declarations.statement:
lemma ker_cfc_le_ker_on_set
    (hs : spectrum ℝ A.mat ⊆ s)
    (h : ∀ i ∈ s, f i = 0 → i = 0) :
    (A.cfc f).ker ≤ A.ker

modules.title: Compound matrices on `HermitianMat`
modules.doc:
This file lifts the compound-matrix construction from
`QuantumInfo.ForMathlib.Majorization` to `HermitianMat`. The compound matrix of
a Hermitian matrix is again Hermitian, and inherits the natural spectral and
positivity properties of the original.

declarations.name: HermitianMat.compoundHermitian
declarations.doc:
The `k`-th compound matrix of a Hermitian matrix, packaged as a
`HermitianMat`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def compoundHermitian (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    HermitianMat {S : Finset d // S.card = k} ℂ

declarations.name: HermitianMat.compoundHermitian_eigenvalues
declarations.doc:
The eigenvalues of `compoundHermitian A k` are the products of eigenvalues
of `A` over `k`-subsets, up to an index permutation.
declarations.statement:
lemma compoundHermitian_eigenvalues (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    ∃ σ : {S : Finset d // S.card = k} ≃ {S : Finset d // S.card = k},
      (compoundHermitian A k).H.eigenvalues ∘ σ =
        fun S => ∏ i : Fin k, A.H.eigenvalues (S.1.orderEmbOfFin S.2 i)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.compoundHermitian_nonneg
declarations.doc: `compoundHermitian` preserves positive semidefiniteness.
declarations.statement:
lemma compoundHermitian_nonneg (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (hA : 0 ≤ A) (k : ℕ) :
    0 ≤ compoundHermitian A k

declarations.name: HermitianMat.compoundHermitian_conj
declarations.doc:
`compoundHermitian` distributes over `HermitianMat.conj`: the compound of
`A.conj B` equals the conjugation of `compoundHermitian A k` by `compoundMatrix B k`.
declarations.statement:
lemma compoundHermitian_conj (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (B : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    compoundHermitian (A.conj B) k =
      (compoundHermitian A k).conj (compoundMatrix B k)

modules.title: Inner product of Hermitian Matrices
modules.doc:
For general matrices there are multiple reasonable notions of "inner product" (Hilbert–Schmidt inner product,
Frobenius inner product), and so Mathlib avoids giving a canonical `InnerProductSpace` instance. But for the
particular case of Hermitian matrices, these all coincide, so we can put a canonical `InnerProductSpace`
instance.

This _does_ however induce a `Norm` on `HermitianMat` as well, the Frobenius norm, and this is less obviously
a uniquely correct choice. It is something that one essentially has to live with, with the way that Mathlib
currently structures the instances. (Thankfully, all norms induce the same _topology and bornology_ on
finite-dimensional matrices.)

Some care to be taken so that the topology induced by the InnerProductSpace is defeq with the Subtype
topology that HermitianMat inherits from the topology on Matrix. This can be done via
`InnerProductSpace.ofCoreOfTopology`.

declarations.doc:
The inner product ⟪A, B⟫ equals ∑_{ij} a_i b_j w_{ij} where a_i, b_j are eigenvalues
and w_{ij} = ‖C_{ij}‖² for C = U_A^* U_B unitary.
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_eq_doubly_stochastic_sum {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    (A B : HermitianMat d ℂ) :
    let C := A.H.eigenvectorUnitary.val.conjTranspose * B.H.eigenvectorUnitary.val
    ⟪A, B⟫_ℝ = ∑ i, ∑ j,
      A.H.eigenvalues i * B.H.eigenvalues j * (‖C i j‖^2)

Hermitian matrices have a Jordan algebra structure given by
`A * B := 2⁻¹ • (A.toMat * B.toMat + B.toMat * A.toMat)`. We call this operation
`HermitianMat.symmMul`, but it's available as `*` multiplication scoped under
`HermMul`. When `A` and `B` commute, this reduces to standard matrix multiplication.

Matrix logarithm (base e) of a Hermitian matrix, as given by the elementwise
real logarithm of the diagonal in a diagonalized form, using `Real.log`

Note that this means that the nullspace of the image includes all of the nullspace of the
original matrix. This contrasts to the standard definition, which is typically defined for
positive *definite* matrices, and the nullspace of the image is exactly the
(λ=1)-eigenspace of the original matrix. (We also get the (λ=-1)-eigenspace here!)

It coincides with a standard definition if A is positive definite.

declarations.name: HermitianMat.logApprox_mono
declarations.doc: Monotonicity of the finite integral approximation of the logarithm.
declarations.statement:
theorem logApprox_mono {x y : HermitianMat d 𝕜} (hx : x.mat.PosDef) (hy : y.mat.PosDef)
    (hxy : x ≤ y) (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    ∫ t in (0)..T, ((1 + t)⁻¹ • (1 : HermitianMat d 𝕜) - (x + t • 1)⁻¹) ≤
    ∫ t in (0)..T, ((1 + t)⁻¹ • (1 : HermitianMat d 𝕜) - (y + t • 1)⁻¹)

declarations.statement: noncomputable def scalarLogApprox (T : ℝ) (u : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.statement:
lemma scalarLogApprox_eq (x T : ℝ) (hx : 0 < x) (hT : 0 < T) :
    scalarLogApprox T x = Real.log x + Real.log ((1 + T) / (x + T))

declarations.name: HermitianMat.logApprox_eq_cfc_scalar
declarations.doc: The matrix log approximation is the CFC of the scalar log approximation.
declarations.statement:
theorem logApprox_eq_cfc_scalar
    (x : HermitianMat d 𝕜) (hx : x.mat.PosDef) (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    logApprox x T = x.cfc (scalarLogApprox T)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.logApprox_eq_log_add_error
declarations.doc: The log approximation is the log plus an error term.
declarations.statement:
theorem logApprox_eq_log_add_error
    (x : HermitianMat d 𝕜) (hx : x.mat.PosDef) (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    logApprox x T = x.log + x.cfc (fun u => Real.log ((1 + T) / (u + T)))

declarations.name: HermitianMat.tendsto_cfc_log_div_add_atTop
declarations.doc: The error term in the log approximation tends to 0 as T goes to infinity.
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_cfc_log_div_add_atTop (x : HermitianMat d 𝕜) :
    Tendsto (fun T => x.cfc (fun u => Real.log ((1 + T) / (u + T)))) atTop (nhds 0)

declarations.statement:

  Tendsto (fun T => logApprox x T) atTop (nhds x.log)

    ⦃a b : ℝ⦄ (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hab : a + b = 1) :
    (a • x + b • y)⁻¹ ≤ a • x⁻¹ + b • y⁻¹

declarations.name: HermitianMat.logApprox_concave
declarations.doc: The finite integral approximation of the matrix logarithm is operator concave.
declarations.statement:
theorem logApprox_concave {n 𝕜 : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [RCLike 𝕜]
    {x y : HermitianMat n 𝕜} (hx : x.mat.PosDef) (hy : y.mat.PosDef)
    ⦃a b : ℝ⦄ (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hab : a + b = 1) (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 ≤ T) :
    a • x.logApprox T + b • y.logApprox T ≤ (a • x + b • y).logApprox T

declarations.name: HermitianMat.log_concave
declarations.doc: The matrix logarithm is operator concave.
declarations.statement:
theorem log_concave {x y : HermitianMat d 𝕜} (hx : x.mat.PosDef) (hy : y.mat.PosDef)
    ⦃a b : ℝ⦄ (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hab : a + b = 1) :
    a • x.log + b • y.log ≤ (a • x + b • y).log

declarations.statement:
lemma log_kron_diagonal {m n 𝕜 : Type*} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [RCLike 𝕜]
    {d₁ : m → ℝ} {d₂ : n → ℝ} (h₁ : ∀ i, 0 < d₁ i) (h₂ : ∀ j, 0 < d₂ j) :
    (diagonal 𝕜 d₁ ⊗ₖ diagonal 𝕜 d₂).log =
    (diagonal 𝕜 d₁).log ⊗ₖ 1 + 1 ⊗ₖ (diagonal 𝕜 d₂).log

declarations.name: HermitianMat.log_kron
declarations.doc:
The matrix logarithm of the Kronecker product of two nonsingular Hermitian matrices is
the sum of the Kronecker products of their logarithms with the identity matrix.
declarations.statement: theorem log_kron [NonSingular A] [NonSingular B] : (A ⊗ₖ B).log = A.log ⊗ₖ 1 + 1 ⊗ₖ B.log

declarations.name: HermitianMat.inv_conj
declarations.statement:
lemma inv_conj [DecidableEq n] {M : Matrix n n 𝕜} (hM : IsUnit M) :
    (A.conj M)⁻¹ = A⁻¹.conj (M⁻¹)ᴴ

declarations.name: HermitianMat.le_iff_mulVec_le_mulVec
declarations.statement:
lemma le_iff_mulVec_le_mulVec (A B : HermitianMat n 𝕜) :
    A ≤ B ↔ ∀ v : n → 𝕜, star v ⬝ᵥ A.mat *ᵥ v ≤ star v ⬝ᵥ B.mat *ᵥ v

declarations.name: HermitianMat.inner_mulVec_nonneg
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_mulVec_nonneg (hA : 0 ≤ A) (v : n → 𝕜) :
    0 ≤ star v ⬝ᵥ A.mat *ᵥ v

declarations.name: HermitianMat.mem_ker_of_inner_mulVec_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_ker_of_inner_mulVec_zero [DecidableEq n] (hA : 0 ≤ A) (v : EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n)
    (h : star v ⬝ᵥ A.mat *ᵥ v = 0) : v ∈ A.ker

declarations.name: HermitianMat.ker_add
declarations.statement:
lemma ker_add [DecidableEq n] (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hB : 0 ≤ B) :
    (A + B).ker = A.ker ⊓ B.ker

declarations.name: HermitianMat.ker_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma ker_sum [DecidableEq n] (f : ι → HermitianMat n 𝕜) (hf : ∀ i, 0 ≤ f i) :
    (∑ i, f i).ker = ⨅ i, (f i).ker

declarations.name: HermitianMat.ker_conj
declarations.statement:
lemma ker_conj [DecidableEq n] (hA : 0 ≤ A) (B : Matrix n n 𝕜) :
    (A.conj B).ker = Submodule.comap (Matrix.toEuclideanLin B.conjTranspose) A.ker

declarations.name: HermitianMat.ker_le_of_le_smul
declarations.statement: lemma ker_le_of_le_smul {α : ℝ} [DecidableEq n] (hα : α ≠ 0) (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hAB : A ≤ α • B) : B.ker ≤ A.ker

declarations.name: HermitianMat.le_smul_one_imp_eigenvalues_le
declarations.doc: If a Hermitian matrix is bounded by `M * I`, then all its eigenvalues are at most `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem le_smul_one_imp_eigenvalues_le [DecidableEq n] (A : HermitianMat n ℂ) (M : ℝ)
    (h : A ≤ M • (1 : HermitianMat n ℂ)) (i : n) :
    A.H.eigenvalues i ≤ M

declarations.name: HermitianMat.eigenvalues_le_imp_le_smul_one
declarations.doc: If all eigenvalues of a Hermitian matrix are at most `M`, then it is bounded by `M * I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eigenvalues_le_imp_le_smul_one [DecidableEq n] (A : HermitianMat n ℂ) (M : ℝ)
    (h : ∀ i, A.H.eigenvalues i ≤ M) :
    A ≤ M • (1 : HermitianMat n ℂ)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.eigenvalues_nonneg
declarations.doc: If a HermitianMat is PSD, then its eigenvalues are nonneg.
declarations.statement:
theorem eigenvalues_nonneg [DecidableEq n] (hA : 0 ≤ A) (i : n) :
    0 ≤ A.H.eigenvalues i

declarations.name: HermitianMat.mat_nonneg
declarations.doc: If a HermitianMat is PSD, its underlying matrix is nonneg in the Loewner order.
declarations.statement: theorem mat_nonneg (hA : 0 ≤ A) : 0 ≤ A.mat

declarations.name: HermitianMat.mat_pos
declarations.doc: If a HermitianMat is positive, its underlying matrix is positive in the Loewner order.
declarations.statement: theorem mat_pos (hA : 0 < A) : 0 < A.mat

declarations.name: Matrix.nonneg_conjTranspose_mul_self
declarations.doc: `Mᴴ * M` is nonneg in the Loewner order, for any matrix `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem _root_.Matrix.nonneg_conjTranspose_mul_self {m : Type*} [Fintype m]
    (M : Matrix m n 𝕜) : 0 ≤ M.conjTranspose * M

declarations.name: Matrix.nonneg_self_mul_conjTranspose
declarations.doc: `M * Mᴴ` is nonneg in the Loewner order, for any matrix `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem _root_.Matrix.nonneg_self_mul_conjTranspose {m : Type*} [Fintype m]
    (M : Matrix n m 𝕜) : 0 ≤ M * M.conjTranspose

declarations.name: HermitianMat.subtype_mk_nonneg
declarations.statement:
lemma subtype_mk_nonneg {M : Matrix m m 𝕜} (h : 0 ≤ M) :
    0 ≤ (⟨M, (Matrix.LE.le.posSemidef h).isHermitian⟩ : HermitianMat m 𝕜)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.subtype_mk_pos
declarations.statement:
lemma subtype_mk_pos {M : Matrix m m 𝕜} (h : 0 < M) :
    0 < (⟨M, (Matrix.LE.le.posSemidef h.le).isHermitian⟩ : HermitianMat m 𝕜)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.evalHermitianMatMat
declarations.doc: Positivity extension for `A.mat` where `A : HermitianMat`: nonneg when `0 ≤ A`.
declarations.statement: meta def evalHermitianMatMat : PositivityExt

declarations.name: HermitianMat.evalHermitianMatVal
declarations.doc: Positivity extension for `A.mat` where `A : HermitianMat`: nonneg when `0 ≤ A`.
declarations.statement: meta def evalHermitianMatVal : PositivityExt

declarations.name: HermitianMat.evalMatrixSelfMulConjTranspose
declarations.doc: Positivity extension for `M * Mᴴ` as a Matrix: always nonneg.
declarations.statement: meta def evalMatrixSelfMulConjTranspose : PositivityExt

declarations.name: HermitianMat.evalMatrixConjTransposeMulSelf
declarations.doc: Positivity extension for `Mᴴ * M` as a Matrix: always nonneg.
declarations.statement: meta def evalMatrixConjTransposeMulSelf : PositivityExt

declarations.name: HermitianMat.evalHermitianMatMk
declarations.doc:
Positivity extension for `⟨M, (pf : M.IsHermitian)⟩` as a HermitianMat:
equivalent to `0 ≤ M` in `MatrixOrder`.
declarations.statement: meta def evalHermitianMatMk : PositivityExt

declarations.name: HermitianMat.evalMatrixEigenvalues
declarations.doc:
Positivity extension for eigenvalues of a Matrix: `0 ≤ (_ : M.IsHermitian).eigenvalues i`.
Will try to prove `0 ≤ M` in the `MatrixOrder`. If the proof is `A.H`, i.e. M comes from a
HermitianMat, this will give `0 ≤ A.mat` which becomes `0 ≤ A` later.
declarations.statement: meta def evalMatrixEigenvalues : PositivityExt

declarations.name: HermitianMat.trace_cfc_conj_unitary
declarations.doc:
The trace of cfc(g, A) is invariant under unitary conjugation of A.
Follows from `cfc_conj_unitary` and `trace_conj_unitary`.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_cfc_conj_unitary (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (g : ℝ → ℝ) (U : 𝐔[d]) :
    ((A.conj U.val).cfc g).trace = (A.cfc g).trace

declarations.name: HermitianMat.peierls_inequality
declarations.doc:
Peierls inequality: for a convex function g, the sum of g applied to the
diagonal entries of a Hermitian matrix is at most the trace of g(A).
This follows from Jensen's inequality applied to the spectral decomposition.
declarations.statement:
theorem peierls_inequality (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (g : ℝ → ℝ) (hg : ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ g) :
    ∑ i, g ((A.mat i i).re) ≤ (A.cfc g).trace

declarations.name: HermitianMat.peierls_inequality_ici
declarations.statement:
lemma peierls_inequality_ici (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (g : ℝ → ℝ) (hg : ConvexOn ℝ (Set.Ici 0) g)
  (hA : 0 ≤ A) :
    ∑ i, g ((A.mat i i).re) ≤ (A.cfc g).trace

declarations.name: HermitianMat.trace_function_convex_univ
declarations.doc:
Joint convexity of the trace functional: for a convex function g,
the map A ↦ tr(g(A)) is convex on the space of Hermitian matrices.
declarations.statement:
theorem trace_function_convex_univ (g : ℝ → ℝ) (hg : ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ g) :
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (fun A : HermitianMat d ℂ => (A.cfc g).trace)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.trace_function_convex_ici
declarations.doc:
Convexity of trace functions: if `g` is convex on `ℝ₊`, then `A ↦ Tr[g(A)]` is
convex on PSD matrices.
declarations.statement:
theorem trace_function_convex_ici {g : ℝ → ℝ} (hg : ConvexOn ℝ (Set.Ici 0) g) :
    ConvexOn ℝ {A : HermitianMat d ℂ | 0 ≤ A} (fun A => (A.cfc g).trace)

modules.title: Projectors associated to Hermitian matrices
modules.doc:
* `projector`: The `HermitianMat` that projects onto a given submodule
 * `supportProj`: The `HermitianMat` that projects onto the range (nonzero eigenvalues)
 * `kerProj`: The `HermitianMat` that projects onto the kernel
 * `projLE`: With notation `{A ≤ₚ B}`, `projLE A B` is the projector onto the nonnegative
   eigenspace of `B - A`.
 * `projLT`: With notation `{A <ₚ B}`, `projLT A B` is the projector onto the positive
   eigenspace of `B - A`.
 * Positive and negative part, written `A⁺` and `A⁻`, give the restriction of a HermitianMat
   onto its positive (resp. negative) eigenvalues; equivalently, it's nonnegative (resp.
   nonpositive) eigenvalues.

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projector
declarations.doc:
Given a Submodule (EuclideanSpace ...) to HermitianMat, this gives the projector onto that subspace,
i.e. a matrix that squares to itself, preserves vectors in the submodule, and zeroes out anything
in the orthogonal complement of that submodule.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def projector (S : Submodule 𝕜 (EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n)) : HermitianMat n 𝕜

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projector_add_orthogonal
declarations.statement: lemma projector_add_orthogonal : projector S + projector Sᗮ = 1

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projector_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma projector_nonneg : 0 ≤ projector S

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projector_ker
declarations.statement: lemma projector_ker : (projector S).ker = Sᗮ

declarations.name: HermitianMat.trace_projector
declarations.statement: lemma trace_projector : (projector S).trace = (Module.finrank 𝕜 S : ℝ)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.supportProj
declarations.doc: The `HermitianMat.projector` for the `HermitianMat.support` submodule.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def supportProj (A : HermitianMat n 𝕜) : HermitianMat n 𝕜

declarations.name: HermitianMat.kerProj
declarations.doc: The `HermitianMat.projector` for the `HermitianMat.ker` submodule.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def kerProj (A : HermitianMat n 𝕜) : HermitianMat n 𝕜

declarations.name: HermitianMat.supportProj_ker
declarations.statement: lemma supportProj_ker : A.supportProj.ker = A.ker

declarations.name: HermitianMat.kerProj_ker
declarations.statement: lemma kerProj_ker : A.kerProj.ker = A.support

declarations.name: HermitianMat.kerProj_add_supportProj
declarations.statement: lemma kerProj_add_supportProj : A.kerProj + A.supportProj = 1

declarations.name: HermitianMat.kerProj_of_nonSingular
declarations.statement: lemma kerProj_of_nonSingular [NonSingular A] : A.kerProj = 0

declarations.name: HermitianMat.supportProj_of_nonSingular
declarations.statement: lemma supportProj_of_nonSingular [NonSingular A] : A.supportProj = 1

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projector_eq_sum_rankOne
declarations.doc: The projector onto a submodule S is the sum of the outer products of the vectors in an orthonormal basis of S.
declarations.statement:
theorem projector_eq_sum_rankOne (b : OrthonormalBasis ι 𝕜 S) :
    (projector S).mat = ∑ i, Matrix.vecMulVec (S.subtype (b i)) (star (S.subtype (b i)))

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projector_support_eq_sum
declarations.doc: The projector onto the support of A is the sum of the projections onto the eigenvectors with non-zero eigenvalues.
declarations.statement:
lemma projector_support_eq_sum : A.supportProj.mat =
    ∑ i, (if A.H.eigenvalues i = 0 then 0 else 1) •
      Matrix.vecMulVec (A.H.eigenvectorBasis i) (star (A.H.eigenvectorBasis i))

declarations.name: HermitianMat.supportProj_eq_cfc
declarations.statement: lemma supportProj_eq_cfc : A.supportProj = A.cfc (if · = 0 then 0 else 1)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projLE
declarations.doc:
Projector onto the non-negative eigenspace of `B - A`. Accessible by the notation
`{A ≤ₚ B}`, which is scoped to `HermitianMat`. This is the unique maximum operator `P`
such that `P^2 = P` and `P * A * P ≤ P * B * P` in the Loewner order.
declarations.statement: def projLE (A B : HermitianMat n 𝕜) : HermitianMat n 𝕜

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projLT
declarations.doc:
Projector onto the positive eigenspace of `B - A`. Accessible by the notation
`{A <ₚ B}`, which is scoped to `HermitianMat`. Compare with `proj_le`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def projLT (A B : HermitianMat n 𝕜) : HermitianMat n 𝕜

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projLE_def
declarations.statement: lemma projLE_def : {A ≤ₚ B} = (B - A).cfc (fun x ↦ if 0 ≤ x then 1 else 0)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projLT_def
declarations.statement: lemma projLT_def : {A <ₚ B} = (B - A).cfc (fun x ↦ if 0 < x then 1 else 0)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projLE_sq
declarations.statement: lemma projLE_sq : {A ≤ₚ B}^2 = {A ≤ₚ B}

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projLT_sq
declarations.statement: lemma projLT_sq : {A <ₚ B}^2 = {A <ₚ B}

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projLE_zero_cfc
declarations.statement: lemma projLE_zero_cfc : {0 ≤ₚ A} = A.cfc (fun x ↦ if 0 ≤ x then 1 else 0)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projLT_zero_cfc
declarations.statement: lemma projLT_zero_cfc : {0 <ₚ A} = A.cfc (fun x ↦ if 0 < x then 1 else 0)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projLE_zero_cfc'
declarations.statement: lemma projLE_zero_cfc' : {A ≤ₚ 0} = A.cfc (fun x ↦ if x ≤ 0 then 1 else 0)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projLT_zero_cfc'
declarations.statement: lemma projLT_zero_cfc' : {A <ₚ 0} = A.cfc (fun x ↦ if x < 0 then 1 else 0)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projLE_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma projLE_nonneg : 0 ≤ {A ≤ₚ B}

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projLT_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma projLT_nonneg : 0 ≤ {A <ₚ B}

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projLE_le_one
declarations.statement: lemma projLE_le_one : {A ≤ₚ B} ≤ 1

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projLE_mul_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma projLE_mul_nonneg : 0 ≤ {A ≤ₚ B}.mat * (B - A).mat

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projLE_mul_le
declarations.statement: lemma projLE_mul_le : {A ≤ₚ B}.mat * A.mat ≤ {A ≤ₚ B}.mat * B.mat

declarations.name: HermitianMat.proj_le_add_lt
declarations.statement: lemma proj_le_add_lt : {A <ₚ B} + {B ≤ₚ A} = 1

declarations.name: HermitianMat.conj_lt_add_conj_le
declarations.statement: lemma conj_lt_add_conj_le : A.conj {A <ₚ 0} + A.conj {0 ≤ₚ A} = A

declarations.name: HermitianMat.supportProj_eq_proj_lt_add_proj_lt
declarations.statement:
lemma supportProj_eq_proj_lt_add_proj_lt (A : HermitianMat n 𝕜) :
    A.supportProj = {A <ₚ 0} + {0 <ₚ A}

declarations.doc: The positive part of a Hermitian matrix: the projection onto its positive eigenvalues.
declarations.statement: instance : PosPart (HermitianMat n 𝕜)

declarations.doc: The negative part of a Hermitian matrix: the projection onto its negative eigenvalues.
declarations.statement: instance : NegPart (HermitianMat n 𝕜)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.posPart_eq_cfc_max
declarations.statement: lemma posPart_eq_cfc_max : A⁺ = A.cfc (fun x ↦ x ⊔ 0)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.negPart_eq_cfc_min
declarations.statement: lemma negPart_eq_cfc_min : A⁻ = A.cfc (fun x ↦ -x ⊔ 0)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.posPart_eq_cfc_ite
declarations.statement: lemma posPart_eq_cfc_ite : A⁺ = A.cfc (fun x ↦ if 0 ≤ x then x else 0)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.negPart_eq_cfc_ite
declarations.statement: lemma negPart_eq_cfc_ite : A⁻ = A.cfc (fun x ↦ if x ≤ 0 then -x else 0)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.posPart_eq_posPart_toMat
declarations.doc:
There is an existing (very slow) `PosPart` instance on `Matrix n n 𝕜`, this shows
that this is equal.
declarations.statement: theorem posPart_eq_posPart_toMat : A⁺ = A.mat⁺

declarations.name: HermitianMat.negPart_eq_negPart_toMat
declarations.doc:
There is an existing (very slow) `PosPart` instance on `Matrix n n 𝕜`, this shows
that this is equal.
declarations.statement: theorem negPart_eq_negPart_toMat : A⁻ = A.mat⁻

declarations.name: HermitianMat.posPart_eq_cfc_lt
declarations.doc: The positive part can be equivalently described as the nonnegative part.
declarations.statement: theorem posPart_eq_cfc_lt : A⁺ = A.cfc (fun x ↦ if 0 < x then x else 0)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.negPart_eq_cfc_lt
declarations.doc: The negative part can be equivalently described as the nonpositive part.
declarations.statement: theorem negPart_eq_cfc_lt : A⁻ = A.cfc (fun x ↦ if x < 0 then -x else 0)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.posPart_add_negPart
declarations.statement: lemma posPart_add_negPart : A⁺ - A⁻ = A

declarations.name: HermitianMat.posPart_eq_self
declarations.statement:
lemma posPart_eq_self {A : HermitianMat n 𝕜} (hA : 0 ≤ A) :
    A⁺ = A

declarations.name: HermitianMat.posPart_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma posPart_nonneg : 0 ≤ A⁺

declarations.name: HermitianMat.negPart_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma negPart_nonneg : 0 ≤ A⁻

declarations.name: HermitianMat.posPart_le
declarations.statement: lemma posPart_le : A ≤ A⁺

declarations.name: HermitianMat.posPart_mul_negPart
declarations.statement: lemma posPart_mul_negPart : A⁺.mat * A⁻.mat = 0

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projLE_inner_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma projLE_inner_nonneg  : 0 ≤ ⟪{A ≤ₚ B}, (B - A)⟫

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projLE_inner_le
declarations.statement: lemma projLE_inner_le : ⟪{A ≤ₚ B}, A⟫ ≤ ⟪{A ≤ₚ B}, B⟫

declarations.name: HermitianMat.inner_projLE_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma inner_projLE_nonneg : 0 ≤ ⟪{A ≤ₚ B}, (B - A)⟫

declarations.name: HermitianMat.inner_projLE_le
declarations.statement: lemma inner_projLE_le : ⟪{A ≤ₚ B}, A⟫ ≤ ⟪{A ≤ₚ B}, B⟫

declarations.name: HermitianMat.posPart_Continuous
declarations.statement: lemma posPart_Continuous : Continuous (·⁺ : HermitianMat n ℂ → _)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.negPart_Continuous
declarations.statement: lemma negPart_Continuous : Continuous (·⁻ : HermitianMat n ℂ → _)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.one_sub_projLT
declarations.statement: lemma one_sub_projLT : 1 - {B ≤ₚ A} = {A <ₚ B}

declarations.name: HermitianMat.projLT_mul_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma projLT_mul_nonneg : 0 ≤ {A <ₚ B}.mat * (B - A).mat

declarations.name: HermitianMat.proj_lt_mul_lt
declarations.statement: lemma proj_lt_mul_lt : {A <ₚ B}.mat * A.mat ≤ {A <ₚ B}.mat * B.mat

declarations.name: HermitianMat.inner_negPart_nonpos
declarations.statement: lemma inner_negPart_nonpos : ⟪A, A⁻⟫ ≤ 0

declarations.name: HermitianMat.posPart_inner_negPart_zero
declarations.statement: lemma posPart_inner_negPart_zero : ⟪A⁺, A⁻⟫ = 0

declarations.name: HermitianMat.inner_negPart_zero_iff
declarations.statement: lemma inner_negPart_zero_iff : ⟪A, A⁻⟫ = 0 ↔ 0 ≤ A

declarations.name: HermitianMat.posPart_eq_zero_iff
declarations.statement: lemma posPart_eq_zero_iff : A⁺ = 0 ↔ A ≤ 0

declarations.name: HermitianMat.inner_negPart_neg_iff
declarations.statement: lemma inner_negPart_neg_iff : ⟪A, A⁻⟫ < 0 ↔ ¬0 ≤ A

declarations.name: HermitianMat.nonneg_iff_inner_nonneg
declarations.doc:
The self-duality of the PSD cone: a matrix is PSD iff its inner product with all
nonnegative matrices is non-negative.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonneg_iff_inner_nonneg (A : HermitianMat n 𝕜) :
    0 ≤ A ↔ ∀ B, 0 ≤ B → 0 ≤ ⟪A, B⟫

modules.doc:
Much like `Matrix.reindex` and `Matrix.submatrix`, we can reindex a Hermitian matrix to get another
Hermitian matrix; however, this only makes sense when both permutations are the same, accordingly,
`HermitianMat.reindex` only takes one `Equiv` argument (as opposed to `Matrix.reindex`'s two).

This file then gives relevant lemmas for simplifying this.

sections.text:
Our simp-normal form for expressions involving `HermitianMat.reindex` is that we try to push
the reindexing as far out as possible, so that it can be absorbed by `HermitianMat.trace`, or
cancelled our in a `HermitianMat.inner`. In places where it commutes (like `HermitianMat.inner`)
we push it to the right side. One downside is that we're not as likely to hit `reindex_one`.

declarations.name: HermitianMat.reindex
declarations.statement: def reindex (e : d ≃ d₂) : HermitianMat d₂ 𝕜

declarations.name: HermitianMat.mat_reindex
declarations.statement: lemma mat_reindex : (A.reindex e).mat = A.mat.reindex e e

declarations.name: HermitianMat.reindex_refl
declarations.statement:
lemma reindex_refl (A : HermitianMat d 𝕜) :
    A.reindex (.refl _) = A

declarations.name: HermitianMat.reindex_reindex
declarations.statement:
lemma reindex_reindex (A : HermitianMat d 𝕜) (e : d ≃ d₂) (f : d₂ ≃ d₃) :
    (A.reindex e).reindex f = A.reindex (e.trans f)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.reindex_zero
declarations.statement: lemma reindex_zero : (0 : HermitianMat d 𝕜).reindex e = 0

declarations.name: HermitianMat.reindex_one
declarations.statement:
lemma reindex_one [DecidableEq d] [DecidableEq d₂] :
    (1 : HermitianMat d 𝕜).reindex e = 1

declarations.name: HermitianMat.reindex_add
declarations.statement: lemma reindex_add : A.reindex e + B.reindex e = (A + B).reindex e

declarations.name: HermitianMat.reindex_sub
declarations.statement: lemma reindex_sub  : A.reindex e - B.reindex e = (A - B).reindex e

declarations.name: HermitianMat.reindex_neg
declarations.statement: lemma reindex_neg : (-A).reindex e = -(A.reindex e)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.reindex_smul
declarations.statement: lemma reindex_smul (c : ℝ) : (c • A).reindex e = c • (A.reindex e)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.reindex_conj
declarations.statement:
lemma reindex_conj [Fintype d₂] [Fintype d] (B : Matrix d₃ d₂ 𝕜) :
    (A.reindex e).conj B = A.conj (B.submatrix id e)

declarations.name: HermitianMat.conj_submatrix
declarations.statement:

modules.title: Matrix Powers With Real Exponents
modules.doc:
This file defines real powers of finite-dimensional Hermitian matrices by continuous
functional calculus:

`A ^ r = A.cfc (fun x => x ^ r)`.

The scalar function is `Real.rpow`, so this is a total operation on Hermitian matrices.
For positive semidefinite matrices it has the expected spectral meaning. For negative
exponents on singular matrices it follows the `Real.rpow` convention, so zero eigenvalues
remain zero; use positive-definiteness hypotheses for inverse laws.

Main results:
* algebraic and spectral lemmas for real powers;
* continuity in the exponent and in the matrix argument;
* the Loewner-Heinz monotonicity theorem for `0 < q <= 1`;
* Lieb-Thirring and Rotfel'd trace inequalities for `0 < p <= 1`.

sections.text:
## Loewner-Heinz Theorem
The operator monotonicity of `x ↦ x ^ q` for `0 < q ≤ 1`:
if `A ≤ B` (in the Loewner order), then `A ^ q ≤ B ^ q`.
This is proved using the resolvent integral representation, following the same
approach as `log_mono` in `LogExp.lean`. The key identity is:
  `x ^ q = c_q * ∫ t in (0,∞), t ^ (q-1) * x / (x + t) dt`
where `c_q = sin(π q) / π`. Since each integrand `x / (x + t)` is operator
monotone (via `inv_antitone`), the integral is operator monotone.

## Araki-Lieb-Thirring Inequality

The next section proves the trace inequality
`Tr[(B ^ r) (A ^ r) (B ^ r)] <= Tr[(B A B) ^ r]` for `0 < r <= 1`.
The proof uses compound matrices to convert the multiplicative singular-value estimates
into a weak log-majorization argument.

## Rotfel'd Trace Subadditivity

For positive semidefinite `A`, `B` and `0 < p <= 1`, Rotfel'd's inequality says
`Tr[(A + B) ^ p] <= Tr[A ^ p] + Tr[B ^ p]`.

The proof here uses the same resolvent-integral representation as Loewner-Heinz, plus
monotonicity of the trace after inserting square roots. A stronger version can be stated
as a majorization theorem.

sections.text: ## Relating schattenNorm to singular values

## Schatten–Hölder inequality

The *Schatten–Hölder inequality* for matrix products:
For matrices `A`, `B` and exponents `r, p, q > 0` with `1/r = 1/p + 1/q`,
the Schatten `r`-norm of the product satisfies
  `‖A * B‖_{S^r} ≤ ‖A‖_{S^p} * ‖B‖_{S^q}`.
This version includes the quasi-norm case (r, p, q < 1).

### Proof sketch

The proof proceeds in three steps:
1. Express Schatten norms in terms of singular values:
   `‖A‖_p = (∑ σᵢ(A)^p)^{1/p}`.
2. Use the **weak log-majorization** of singular values of products
   (`weakLogMaj_singularValues_mul` + `sum_rpow_le_of_weakLogMaj`) to obtain
   `∑ σᵢ(AB)^r ≤ ∑ σ↓ᵢ(A)^r · σ↓ᵢ(B)^r`.
3. Apply the **classical Hölder inequality** for finite sums
   (`NNReal.inner_le_Lp_mul_Lq` from Mathlib, with conjugate exponents
   `p/r` and `q/r`) to bound
   `∑ σ↓ᵢ(A)^r · σ↓ᵢ(B)^r ≤ (∑ σᵢ(A)^p)^{r/p} · (∑ σᵢ(B)^q)^{r/q}`.
4. Take `1/r`-th powers and combine.

declarations.name: schattenNorm
declarations.doc: The Schatten p-norm of a matrix A is (Tr[(A*A)^(p/2)])^(1/p).
declarations.statement: noncomputable def schattenNorm (A : Matrix d d ℂ) (p : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: schattenNorm_hermitian_pow
declarations.statement:
lemma schattenNorm_hermitian_pow {A : HermitianMat d ℂ} (hA : 0 ≤ A) {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) :
    schattenNorm A.mat p = (A ^ p).trace ^ (1/p)

declarations.name: schattenNorm_nonneg
declarations.statement:
lemma schattenNorm_nonneg (A : Matrix d d ℂ) (p : ℝ) :
    0 ≤ schattenNorm A p

lemma schattenNorm_pow_eq
  (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (hA : 0 ≤ A) (p k : ℝ) (hp : 0 < p) (hk : 0 < k) :
    schattenNorm (A ^ k).mat p = (schattenNorm A.mat (k * p)) ^ k

    (A : HermitianMat d ℂ) (hA : 0 ≤ A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) :
    (A ^ r).trace = (schattenNorm A.mat r) ^ r

declarations.statement:

    RCLike.re ((Matrix.isHermitian_mul_conjTranspose_self A.conjTranspose).cfc (· ^ (p/2))).trace =
    ∑ i : d, ((Matrix.isHermitian_mul_conjTranspose_self A.conjTranspose).eigenvalues i) ^ (p/2)

    schattenNorm A p ^ p = ∑ i : d, singularValues A i ^ p

lemma schattenNorm_eq_sum_singularValues_rpow (A : Matrix d d ℂ) {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) :
    schattenNorm A p = (∑ i : d, singularValues A i ^ p) ^ (1/p)

    schattenNorm A p ^ p =
    ∑ i : Fin (Fintype.card d), singularValuesSorted A i ^ p

modules.title: Trace of Hermitian Matrices
modules.doc:
While the trace of a Hermitian matrix is, in informal math, typically just "the same as" a trace of
a matrix that happens to be Hermitian - it is a real number, not a complex number. Or more generally,
it is a self-adjoint element of the base `StarAddMonoid`.

Working directly with `Matrix.trace` then means that there would be constant casts between rings,
chasing imaginary parts and inequalities and so on. By defining `HermitianMat.trace` as its own
operation, we encapsulate the mess and give a clean interface.

The `IsMaximalSelfAdjoint` class is used so that (for example) for matrices over ℤ or ℝ,
`HermitianMat.trace` works as well and is in fact defeq to `Matrix.trace`. For ℂ or `RCLike`,
it uses the real part.

declarations.name: HermitianMat.trace
declarations.doc:
The trace of the matrix. This requires a `IsMaximalSelfAdjoint R α` instance, and then maps from
`HermitianMat n α` to `R`. This means that the trace of (say) a `HermitianMat n ℤ` gives values in ℤ,
but that the trace of a `HermitianMat n ℂ` gives values in ℝ. The fact that traces are "automatically"
real reduces coercions down the line.
declarations.statement: def trace (A : HermitianMat n α) : R

modules.title: Maximal self-adjoint subrings
modules.doc:
This file introduces the `IsMaximalSelfAdjoint R α` typeclass, which records that the
`TrivialStar` ring `R` carries the self-adjoint part of a star ring `α`. It bundles an
additive, `R`-linear map `selfadjMap : α →+ R` that inverts `algebraMap R α` on self-adjoint
elements. The guiding example is `R = ℝ`, `α = ℂ`: it lets a quantity such as the trace of a
Hermitian matrix be valued in `ℝ` instead of `ℂ`, reflecting that physical observables are
self-adjoint and take real expectation values.

declarations.name: IsMaximalSelfAdjoint
declarations.doc:
`IsMaximalSelfAdjoint R α` witnesses that `R` is the maximal `TrivialStar` subring of the
star ring `α`, via an additive map `selfadjMap : α →+ R` collecting the self-adjoint part of
each element. This lets `HermitianMat.trace` return `𝕜` when `𝕜` already has a trivial star,
and the "clean" underlying type otherwise, e.g. `ℝ` when the input field is `ℂ`.
declarations.statement:
class IsMaximalSelfAdjoint (R : outParam Type*) (α : Type*) [Star α] [Star R] [CommSemiring R]
    [Semiring α] [TrivialStar R] [Algebra R α] where
  /-- The additive map sending an element of `α` to its self-adjoint part in `R`. -/
  selfadjMap : α →+ R
  /-- `selfadjMap` pulls scalar multiplication by `R` out of its argument. -/
  selfadj_smul : ∀ (r : R) (a : α), selfadjMap (r • a) = r * (selfadjMap a)
  /-- On self-adjoint elements, `selfadjMap` is a section of `algebraMap R α`. -/
  selfadj_algebra : ∀ {a : α}, IsSelfAdjoint a → algebraMap _ _ (selfadjMap a) = a

declarations.name: Matrix.Isometry
declarations.doc:
An isometry is a matrix `A` such that `AAᴴ = 1`. Compare with a unitary, which
requires `AAᴴ = AᴴA = 1`. It is common to claim that, in a finite-dimensional vector
space, a two-sided isometry (`A.Isometry ∧ Aᴴ.Isometry`) must be square and therefore unitary;
this is does not work out so well here, since a `Matrix m n R` can be a two-sided isometry,
but cannot be a `unitary` since the rows and columns are index by different labels.

declarations.doc:
If a matrix is diagonalized by a unitary matrix, then it can be written as a
CFC of a (particular, canonical) diagonal matrix.
declarations.statement:
theorem Matrix.IsDiag.exists_cfc {U : Matrix.unitaryGroup d 𝕜} {M : Matrix d d 𝕜}
  (hU : (U.val * M * Uᴴ).IsDiag) (hM : M.IsHermitian) (e : d ≃ Fin (Fintype.card d)) :
       ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ,
    M = cfc f (Uᴴ * (Matrix.diagonal fun x => ↑↑(e x)) * U.val)

declarations.name: Commute.exists_cfc

    ∃ C : Matrix d d 𝕜, (∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, A = cfc f C) ∧ (∃ g : ℝ → ℝ, B = cfc g C)

declarations.name: exists_strictMono_seq_le
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_strictMono_seq_le (y : ℝ≥0) (f : ℝ≥0 → ℕ → ℝ≥0∞) (hf : ∀ x > 0, Filter.atTop.liminf (f x) ≤ y) :
    ∃ n : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono n ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, f ((k : ℝ≥0) + 1)⁻¹ (n k) ≤ (y : ℝ≥0∞) + ((k : ℝ≥0) + 1)⁻¹

    ∃ M : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono M ∧ ∀ k, ∀ n ≥ M k, f ((k + 1 : ℝ≥0)⁻¹) n ≤ y + (k + 1 : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹

Sort of dual to `ENNReal.tendsto_const_sub_nhds_zero_iff`. Takes a substantially different form though, since
we don't actually have equality of the limits, or even the fact that the other one converges, which is why we

modules.title: Relabelling linear equivalences
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

This module provides linear equivalences obtained by relabelling the index type of a finite
function space `d → R` or of `EuclideanSpace 𝕜 d` along an index equivalence `e : d ≃ d₂`,
together with lemmas relating them to `Matrix.reindex`.

## ii. Key results

- `LinearEquiv.ofRelabel` : the `R`-linear equivalence `(d₂ → R) ≃ₗ[R] (d → R)` induced by an
  index equivalence `e : d ≃ d₂`.
- `LinearEquiv.euclideanOfRelabel` : the `EuclideanSpace` analogue of `ofRelabel`.
- `Matrix.reindex_toLin'` and `Matrix.reindex_toEuclideanLin` : reindexing a matrix conjugates
  its associated linear map by these relabelling equivalences.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Relabelling linear equivalences
- B. Reindexing matrices and their linear maps

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: Majorization and weak log-majorization
modules.doc:
This file develops the theory of majorization for finite sequences, leading to
the key singular value inequality needed for the Schatten–Hölder inequality.

## Main results

* `sum_rpow_singularValues_mul_le`: for `r > 0`, the singular values of `A * B`
  satisfy `∑ σᵢ(AB)^r ≤ ∑ σ↓ᵢ(A)^r · σ↓ᵢ(B)^r`.
* `holder_step_for_singularValues`: the Hölder step giving
  `∑ σ↓ᵢ(A)^r · σ↓ᵢ(B)^r ≤ (∑ σᵢ(A)^p)^{r/p} · (∑ σᵢ(B)^q)^{r/q}`.

sections.text: ## Sorted singular values
## Weak log-majorization and its consequences

### Compound matrices and auxiliary lemmas for Horn's inequality

The proof of Horn's inequality uses the *compound matrix* (or *k-th exterior power*
of a matrix).  For a `d × d` matrix `M` and `k ≤ card d`, the `k`-th compound matrix
`C_k(M)` is indexed by `k`-element subsets of the index type, with entry `(S, T)` being
the minor `det M[S, T]`.

The key properties are:
1. **Cauchy–Binet**: `C_k(M N) = C_k(M) · C_k(N)`.
2. **Spectral characterisation**: the largest singular value of `C_k(M)` is
   `∏_{i=1}^k σ↓ᵢ(M)`.
3. **Operator-norm submultiplicativity**: `σ₁(A B) ≤ σ₁(A) · σ₁(B)`.

Combining these gives Horn's inequality:
  `∏ σ↓(AB) = σ₁(C_k(AB)) = σ₁(C_k(A) C_k(B)) ≤ σ₁(C_k(A)) σ₁(C_k(B))
            = (∏ σ↓(A))(∏ σ↓(B))`.
