declarations.name: singularValues
declarations.doc:
The singular values of a square complex matrix `A`, defined as the square
roots of the eigenvalues of `A†A`. These are indexed by `d` without a
particular ordering.

Note: We use `A.conjTranspose` as the argument to `isHermitian_mul_conjTranspose_self`
so that the underlying Hermitian matrix is `A† * A` (matching the convention in `schattenNorm`).
declarations.statement: def singularValues (A : Matrix d d ℂ) : d → ℝ

declarations.name: singularValues_nonneg
declarations.doc: Singular values are nonneg.
declarations.statement:
lemma singularValues_nonneg (A : Matrix d d ℂ) (i : d) :
    0 ≤ singularValues A i

declarations.name: singularValuesSorted
declarations.doc:
The sorted singular values of a square complex matrix, in decreasing order,
indexed by `Fin (Fintype.card d)`.

We define them by sorting the multiset of singular values.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def singularValuesSorted (A : Matrix d d ℂ) :
    Fin (Fintype.card d) → ℝ

declarations.name: singularValuesSorted_nonneg
declarations.doc: Sorted singular values are nonneg.
declarations.statement:
lemma singularValuesSorted_nonneg (A : Matrix d d ℂ) (i : Fin (Fintype.card d)) :
    0 ≤ singularValuesSorted A i

declarations.name: sum_singularValues_rpow_eq_sum_sorted
declarations.doc: The sum `∑ singularValues A i ^ p` equals the sum over sorted singular values.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_singularValues_rpow_eq_sum_sorted (A : Matrix d d ℂ) (p : ℝ) :
    ∑ i : d, singularValues A i ^ p =
    ∑ i : Fin (Fintype.card d), singularValuesSorted A i ^ p

declarations.name: singularValuesSorted_antitone
declarations.doc: Sorted singular values are antitone (decreasing).
declarations.statement:
lemma singularValuesSorted_antitone (A : Matrix d d ℂ) :
    Antitone (singularValuesSorted A)

declarations.name: antitone_mul_of_antitone_nonneg
declarations.doc: The product of nonneg antitone sequences is antitone.
declarations.statement:
lemma antitone_mul_of_antitone_nonneg {n : ℕ}
    {f g : Fin n → ℝ} (hf : Antitone f) (hg : Antitone g)
    (hf_nn : ∀ i, 0 ≤ f i) (hg_nn : ∀ i, 0 ≤ g i) :
    Antitone (fun i => f i * g i)

declarations.name: AllOrdered.fintypeLinearOrderClassical
declarations.doc: A `LinearOrder` on any `Fintype`, obtained classically via well-ordering.
declarations.statement:
scoped instance fintypeLinearOrderClassical (α : Type*) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
    LinearOrder α

declarations.name: compoundMatrix
declarations.doc: The `k`-th compound (exterior-power) matrix of `M`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def compoundMatrix (M : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    Matrix {S : Finset d // S.card = k} {S : Finset d // S.card = k} ℂ

declarations.name: cauchyBinet
declarations.doc:
**Cauchy–Binet formula** for rectangular matrices: if `A` is `m × n` and `B` is
`n × m`, then `det(A * B) = ∑_S det(A[:,S]) * det(B[S,:])` where the sum is
over `m`-element subsets `S` of the column/row index.
declarations.statement:
lemma cauchyBinet {m : ℕ} {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [LinearOrder n]
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (A : Matrix (Fin m) n R) (B : Matrix n (Fin m) R) :
    (A * B).det = ∑ S : {S : Finset n // S.card = m},
      (A.submatrix id (S.1.orderEmbOfFin S.2)).det *
      (B.submatrix (S.1.orderEmbOfFin S.2) id).det

declarations.name: compoundMatrix_mul
declarations.doc: The `compoundMatrix` of a product is the product of the `compoundMatrix`s.
declarations.statement:
lemma compoundMatrix_mul (M N : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    compoundMatrix (M * N) k = compoundMatrix M k * compoundMatrix N k

declarations.name: compoundMatrix_conjTranspose
declarations.doc: `compoundMatrix` commutes with `conjTranspose`.
declarations.statement:
lemma compoundMatrix_conjTranspose (M : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    compoundMatrix M.conjTranspose k = (compoundMatrix M k).conjTranspose

declarations.name: compoundMatrix_diagonal
declarations.doc:
The compound matrix of a diagonal matrix is diagonal, with entries being
products of eigenvalues over k-subsets.
declarations.statement:
lemma compoundMatrix_diagonal (f : d → ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    compoundMatrix (Matrix.diagonal f) k =
    Matrix.diagonal (fun S : {S : Finset d // S.card = k} =>
      ∏ i : Fin k, f (S.1.orderEmbOfFin S.2 i))

declarations.name: compoundMatrix_unitary
declarations.doc: The compound matrix of a unitary matrix is unitary.
declarations.statement:
lemma compoundMatrix_unitary (U : Matrix d d ℂ)
    (hU : U ∈ Matrix.unitaryGroup d ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    compoundMatrix U k ∈ Matrix.unitaryGroup {S : Finset d // S.card = k} ℂ

declarations.name: compoundUnitary
declarations.doc: The `k`-th compound matrix bundled as a unitary.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def compoundUnitary (U : Matrix.unitaryGroup d ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    Matrix.unitaryGroup {S : Finset d // S.card = k} ℂ

declarations.name: compound_card_pos
declarations.doc: The index set of the `k`-th compound matrix is nonempty when `k ≤ card d`.
declarations.statement:
lemma compound_card_pos (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card d) :
    0 < Fintype.card {S : Finset d // S.card = k}

declarations.name: compoundZero
declarations.doc:
The canonical zero index in `Fin (Fintype.card {S : Finset d // S.card = k})`,
witnessed by `compound_card_pos`.
declarations.statement:
def compoundZero (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card d) :
    Fin (Fintype.card {S : Finset d // S.card = k})

declarations.name: singularValues_compoundMatrix_eq
declarations.doc:
The eigenvalues of the compound matrix of a Hermitian matrix are the products
of eigenvalues over k-subsets. More precisely, the singular values of
`compoundMatrix M k` are the square roots of products of eigenvalues of M†M
over k-subsets.
declarations.statement:
lemma singularValues_compoundMatrix_eq (M : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    ∀ (S : {S : Finset d // S.card = k}),
    ∃ (j : {S : Finset d // S.card = k}),
    singularValues (compoundMatrix M k) j =
    ∏ i : Fin k, singularValues M (S.1.orderEmbOfFin S.2 i)

declarations.name: prod_le_prod_sorted
declarations.doc:
The product of nonneg values over a k-subset is at most the product of the
k largest values.
declarations.statement:
lemma prod_le_prod_sorted {n : ℕ} {f : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hf : Antitone f) (hf_nn : ∀ i, 0 ≤ f i)
    (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n)
    (g : Fin k → Fin n) (hg : Function.Injective g) :
    ∏ i : Fin k, f (g i) ≤ ∏ i : Fin k, f ⟨i.val, by omega⟩

declarations.name: singularValuesSorted_zero_eq_sup
declarations.doc: The 0th sorted singular value is the maximum of the singular values.
declarations.statement:
lemma singularValuesSorted_zero_eq_sup {e : Type*} [Fintype e] [DecidableEq e]
    (A : Matrix e e ℂ) (h : 0 < Fintype.card e) :
    singularValuesSorted A ⟨0, h⟩ = Finset.sup' Finset.univ
      (Finset.univ_nonempty_iff.mpr (Fintype.card_pos_iff.mp h))
      (singularValues A)

declarations.name: singularValues_mem_sorted
declarations.doc: Each singular value appears in the sorted list.
declarations.statement:
lemma singularValues_mem_sorted {e : Type*} [Fintype e] [DecidableEq e]
    (A : Matrix e e ℂ) (i : e) :
    ∃ j : Fin (Fintype.card e), singularValues A i = singularValuesSorted A j

declarations.name: singularValuesSorted_mem_values
declarations.doc: Each sorted singular value appears among the original singular values.
declarations.statement:
lemma singularValuesSorted_mem_values {e : Type*} [Fintype e] [DecidableEq e]
    (A : Matrix e e ℂ) (j : Fin (Fintype.card e)) :
    ∃ i : e, singularValuesSorted A j = singularValues A i

declarations.name: singularValues_compoundMatrix_perm
declarations.doc: Stronger version of `singularValues_compoundMatrix_eq` that exposes the permutation.
declarations.statement:
lemma singularValues_compoundMatrix_perm (M : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    ∃ σ : {S : Finset d // S.card = k} ≃ {S : Finset d // S.card = k},
    ∀ S, singularValues (compoundMatrix M k) (σ S) =
    ∏ i : Fin k, singularValues M (S.1.orderEmbOfFin S.2 i)

declarations.name: singularValues_compoundMatrix_rev
declarations.doc:
Converse of `singularValues_compoundMatrix_eq`: every singular value of the
compound matrix is a product of singular values of M over some k-subset.
declarations.statement:
lemma singularValues_compoundMatrix_rev (M : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ)
    (j : {S : Finset d // S.card = k}) :
    ∃ (S : {S : Finset d // S.card = k}),
    singularValues (compoundMatrix M k) j =
    ∏ i : Fin k, singularValues M (S.1.orderEmbOfFin S.2 i)

declarations.name: exists_sorting_equiv
declarations.doc:
There exists a bijection `σ : Fin (card d) ≃ d` such that
`singularValues M (σ i) = singularValuesSorted M i` for all `i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_sorting_equiv (M : Matrix d d ℂ) :
    ∃ σ : Fin (Fintype.card d) ≃ d,
    ∀ i, singularValues M (σ i) = singularValuesSorted M i

declarations.name: prod_singularValues_subset_le_sorted_prod
declarations.doc:
For any k-subset S of d, the product of singular values over S is ≤ the
product of the top k sorted singular values.
declarations.statement:
lemma prod_singularValues_subset_le_sorted_prod (M : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ)
    (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card d) (S : {S : Finset d // S.card = k}) :
    ∏ i : Fin k, singularValues M (S.1.orderEmbOfFin S.2 i) ≤
    ∏ i : Fin k, singularValuesSorted M ⟨i.val, by omega⟩

declarations.name: exists_subset_prod_eq_sorted_prod
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_subset_prod_eq_sorted_prod (M : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ)
    (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card d) :
    ∃ S : {S : Finset d // S.card = k},
    ∏ i : Fin k, singularValues M (S.1.orderEmbOfFin S.2 i) =
    ∏ i : Fin k, singularValuesSorted M ⟨i.val, by omega⟩

declarations.name: prod_singularValuesSorted_eq_compoundSV
declarations.statement:
lemma prod_singularValuesSorted_eq_compoundSV (M : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ)
    (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card d) :
    ∏ i : Fin k, singularValuesSorted M ⟨i.val, by omega⟩ =
    singularValuesSorted (compoundMatrix M k) ⟨0, by
      have : Fintype.card {S : Finset d // S.card = k} = (Fintype.card d).choose k := by
        simp [Fintype.card_subtype]
      rw [this]; exact Nat.choose_pos hk⟩

declarations.name: IsHermitian.inner_le_sup_eigenvalue_mul_inner
declarations.doc:
The **Rayleigh quotient bound**:
For a Hermitian matrix H with eigenvalues λ, we have
`v† H v ≤ (max λ) · v† v` for all v.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsHermitian.inner_le_sup_eigenvalue_mul_inner
    {e : Type*} [Fintype e] [DecidableEq e]
    (H : Matrix e e ℂ) (hH : H.IsHermitian)
    (he : 0 < Fintype.card e)
    (v : e → ℂ) :
    Complex.re (star v ⬝ᵥ H.mulVec v) ≤
    Finset.sup' Finset.univ
      (Finset.univ_nonempty_iff.mpr (Fintype.card_pos_iff.mp he))
      hH.eigenvalues * Complex.re (star v ⬝ᵥ v)

declarations.name: eigenvalue_le_singularValuesSorted_sq
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenvalue_le_singularValuesSorted_sq {e : Type*} [Fintype e] [DecidableEq e]
    (A : Matrix e e ℂ) (h : 0 < Fintype.card e) (i : e) :
  (isHermitian_mul_conjTranspose_self A.conjTranspose).eigenvalues i ≤
    (singularValuesSorted A ⟨0, h⟩) ^ 2

declarations.name: quadratic_form_le_singularValuesSorted_sq
declarations.doc: The quadratic form of `A† A` is bounded by (max singular value)² * ‖v‖².
declarations.statement:
lemma quadratic_form_le_singularValuesSorted_sq {e : Type*} [Fintype e] [DecidableEq e]
    (A : Matrix e e ℂ) (h : 0 < Fintype.card e) (v : e → ℂ) :
  Complex.re (star v ⬝ᵥ (A.conjTranspose * A).mulVec v) ≤
    (singularValuesSorted A ⟨0, h⟩) ^ 2 * Complex.re (star v ⬝ᵥ v)

declarations.name: singularValuesSorted_mul_le
declarations.doc:
The largest singular value of a matrix product is at most the product of the
largest singular values: `σ₁(M * N) ≤ σ₁(M) * σ₁(N)`.
This is operator-norm submultiplicativity.
declarations.statement:
lemma singularValuesSorted_mul_le {e : Type*} [Fintype e] [DecidableEq e]
    (M N : Matrix e e ℂ) (h : 0 < Fintype.card e) :
    singularValuesSorted (M * N) ⟨0, h⟩ ≤
    singularValuesSorted M ⟨0, h⟩ * singularValuesSorted N ⟨0, h⟩

declarations.name: horn_weak_log_majorization
declarations.doc:
Horn's inequality (weak log-majorization of singular values):
For all `k`, `∏_{i<k} σ↓ᵢ(AB) ≤ ∏_{i<k} σ↓ᵢ(A) · σ↓ᵢ(B)`.
This follows from submultiplicativity of the operator norm applied to
exterior powers of the matrices.
declarations.statement:
lemma horn_weak_log_majorization (A B : Matrix d d ℂ) (k : ℕ)
    (hk : k ≤ Fintype.card d) :
    ∏ i : Fin k, singularValuesSorted (A * B) ⟨i.val, by omega⟩ ≤
    ∏ i : Fin k, (singularValuesSorted A ⟨i.val, by omega⟩ *
                   singularValuesSorted B ⟨i.val, by omega⟩)

declarations.name: rpow_antitone_of_nonneg_antitone
declarations.doc: Raising nonneg antitone sequences to a positive power preserves antitonicity.
declarations.statement:
lemma rpow_antitone_of_nonneg_antitone {n : ℕ}
    {f : Fin n → ℝ} (hf : Antitone f) (hf_nn : ∀ i, 0 ≤ f i)
    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
    Antitone (fun i => f i ^ r)

declarations.name: rpow_preserves_weak_log_maj
declarations.doc: Weak log-majorization is preserved under positive powers.
declarations.statement:
lemma rpow_preserves_weak_log_maj {n : ℕ}
    {x y : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hx_nn : ∀ i, 0 ≤ x i) (hy_nn : ∀ i, 0 ≤ y i)
    (h_log_maj : ∀ (k : ℕ) (_ : k ≤ n),
      ∏ i : Fin k, x ⟨i.val, by omega⟩ ≤
      ∏ i : Fin k, y ⟨i.val, by omega⟩)
    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (_ : k ≤ n),
      ∏ i : Fin k, (fun j => x j ^ r) ⟨i.val, by omega⟩ ≤
      ∏ i : Fin k, (fun j => y j ^ r) ⟨i.val, by omega⟩

declarations.name: sum_mul_log_nonneg_of_weak_log_maj
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_mul_log_nonneg_of_weak_log_maj {n : ℕ}
    {x y : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hx_pos : ∀ i, 0 < x i) (hy_pos : ∀ i, 0 < y i)
    (hx_anti : Antitone x)
    (h_log_maj : ∀ (k : ℕ) (_ : k ≤ n),
      ∏ i : Fin k, x ⟨i.val, by omega⟩ ≤
      ∏ i : Fin k, y ⟨i.val, by omega⟩) :
    0 ≤ ∑ i, x i * Real.log (y i / x i)

declarations.name: sub_ge_mul_log_div
declarations.statement:
lemma sub_ge_mul_log_div {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) :
    b - a ≥ a * Real.log (b / a)

declarations.name: weak_log_maj_sum_le
declarations.statement:
lemma weak_log_maj_sum_le {n : ℕ}
    {x y : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hx_nn : ∀ i, 0 ≤ x i) (hy_nn : ∀ i, 0 ≤ y i)
    (hx_anti : Antitone x) (hy_anti : Antitone y)
    (h_log_maj : ∀ (k : ℕ) (_ : k ≤ n),
      ∏ i : Fin k, x ⟨i.val, by omega⟩ ≤
      ∏ i : Fin k, y ⟨i.val, by omega⟩) :
    ∑ i, x i ≤ ∑ i, y i

declarations.name: weak_log_maj_sum_rpow_le
declarations.doc:
Weak log-majorization of nonneg antitone sequences implies the sum of
powers inequality.
declarations.statement:
lemma weak_log_maj_sum_rpow_le {n : ℕ}
    {x y : Fin n → ℝ}
    (hx_nn : ∀ i, 0 ≤ x i) (hy_nn : ∀ i, 0 ≤ y i)
    (hx_anti : Antitone x) (hy_anti : Antitone y)
    (h_log_maj : ∀ (k : ℕ) (_ : k ≤ n),
      ∏ i : Fin k, x ⟨i.val, by omega⟩ ≤
      ∏ i : Fin k, y ⟨i.val, by omega⟩)
    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
    ∑ i, x i ^ r ≤ ∑ i, y i ^ r

declarations.name: sum_rpow_singularValues_mul_le
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_rpow_singularValues_mul_le (A B : Matrix d d ℂ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
    ∑ i : Fin (Fintype.card d), singularValuesSorted (A * B) i ^ r ≤
    ∑ i : Fin (Fintype.card d),
      (singularValuesSorted A i ^ r * singularValuesSorted B i ^ r)

declarations.name: holder_step_for_singularValues
declarations.doc:
The finite-sum Hölder inequality applied to sequences of r-th powers of
sorted singular values.

With conjugate exponents `p' = p/r > 1` and `q' = q/r > 1` (which satisfy
`1/p' + 1/q' = 1` when `1/r = 1/p + 1/q`), this gives:
  `∑ σ↓ᵢ(A)^r · σ↓ᵢ(B)^r ≤ (∑ σ↓ᵢ(A)^p)^{r/p} · (∑ σ↓ᵢ(B)^q)^{r/q}`

Note: The sums on the RHS don't depend on the ordering, so we can replace
sorted singular values with unsorted ones.
declarations.statement:
lemma holder_step_for_singularValues (A B : Matrix d d ℂ)
    {r p q : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (hp : 0 < p) (hq : 0 < q)
    (hpqr : 1 / r = 1 / p + 1 / q) :
    (∑ i : Fin (Fintype.card d),
      (singularValuesSorted A i ^ r * singularValuesSorted B i ^ r)) ≤
    (∑ i : Fin (Fintype.card d), singularValuesSorted A i ^ p) ^ (r / p) *
    (∑ i : Fin (Fintype.card d), singularValuesSorted B i ^ q) ^ (r / q)

declarations.name: Matrix.IsHermitian.cfc_eigenvalues

    ∃ (e : d ≃ d), Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues (cfc_predicate f M) = f ∘ hM.eigenvalues ∘ e

declarations.name: Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues_eq_of_unitary_similarity_diagonal
declarations.doc: If a Hermitian matrix A is unitarily similar to a diagonal matrix with real entries f, then the eigenvalues of A are a permutation of f.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsHermitian.eigenvalues_eq_of_unitary_similarity_diagonal {d 𝕜 : Type*}
    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] [RCLike 𝕜]
    {A : Matrix d d 𝕜} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
    {U : Matrix d d 𝕜} (hU : U ∈ Matrix.unitaryGroup d 𝕜)
    {f : d → ℝ}
    (h : A = U * Matrix.diagonal (fun i => (RCLike.ofReal (f i) : 𝕜)) * Matrix.conjTranspose U) :
    ∃ σ : d ≃ d, hA.eigenvalues ∘ σ = f

declarations.name: Matrix.cfc_diagonal

declarations.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.pow_mul

lemma PosSemidef.pow_mul {A : Matrix d d 𝕜} {x y : ℝ} (hA : A.PosSemidef) :

declarations.name: Matrix.traceRight_eq_traceLeft_reindex
declarations.doc: The right partial trace of a matrix is equal to the left partial trace of the matrix reindexed by swapping the tensor factors.
declarations.statement:
theorem traceRight_eq_traceLeft_reindex {n m R : Type*} [Fintype m] [AddCommMonoid R]
  (M : Matrix (n × m) (n × m) R) :
    M.traceRight = (M.reindex (.prodComm ..) (.prodComm ..)).traceLeft

lemma traceLeft_smul {A : Matrix (m × n) (m × n) α} (r : R) :

lemma unitaryGroup_row_norm [Fintype n] (U : Matrix.unitaryGroup n ℂ) (i : n) :

declarations.name: Matrix.submatrix_eq_mul_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma submatrix_eq_mul_mul {d d₂ d₃ R : Type*} [DecidableEq d] [Fintype d] [Semiring R]
  (A : Matrix d d R) (e : d₂ → d) (f : d₃ → d) :
    A.submatrix e f = (submatrix (α := R) 1 e id : Matrix d₂ d R) * A * (submatrix (α := R) 1 id f)

declarations.name: Matrix.kronecker_conj_eq
declarations.doc: The conjugate of a Kronecker product by a Kronecker product is the Kronecker product of the conjugates (for matrices).
declarations.statement:
lemma kronecker_conj_eq {m n p q α : Type*} [CommSemiring α] [StarRing α] [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
    (A : Matrix m m α) (B : Matrix n n α) (C : Matrix p m α) (D : Matrix q n α) :
    (C ⊗ₖ D) * (A ⊗ₖ B) * (C ⊗ₖ D)ᴴ = (C * A * Cᴴ) ⊗ₖ (D * B * Dᴴ)

declarations.name: Matrix.traceNorm
declarations.doc: The trace norm of a matrix: Tr[√(A† A)].
declarations.statement: def traceNorm (A : Matrix m n R) : ℝ

declarations.name: Matrix.traceNorm_zero
declarations.statement: lemma traceNorm_zero : traceNorm (0 : Matrix m n R) = 0

declarations.name: Matrix.traceNorm_neg
declarations.doc: The trace norm of the negative is equal to the trace norm.
declarations.statement: theorem traceNorm_neg (A : Matrix m n R) : traceNorm (-A) = traceNorm A

declarations.name: Matrix.traceNorm_isometry_left
declarations.doc: The trace norm is invariant under left multiplication by an isometry.
declarations.statement:
theorem traceNorm_isometry_left [Fintype k] {A : Matrix n m R} {u : Matrix k n R}
  (hu₁ : u.Isometry) : traceNorm (u * A) = traceNorm A

declarations.name: Matrix.traceNorm_isometry_right
declarations.doc: The trace norm is invariant under right multiplication by the adjoint of an isometry.
declarations.statement:
theorem traceNorm_isometry_right [Fintype k] {A : Matrix n m R} {u : Matrix k m R}
  (hu₁ : u.Isometry) : traceNorm (A * uᴴ) = traceNorm A

declarations.name: Matrix.traceNorm_unitary_conj
declarations.doc: The trace norm is invariant under unitary conjugation.
declarations.statement:
theorem traceNorm_unitary_conj {A : Matrix n n R} {U : Matrix.unitaryGroup n R} :
  traceNorm (U.val * A * U.valᴴ) = traceNorm A

declarations.name: Matrix.traceNorm_Hermitian_eq_sum_abs_eigenvalues
declarations.doc:
For Hermitian matrices, the trace norm is the sum of absolute eigenvalues.

This is Proposition 9.1.1 in Wilde.
declarations.statement:
theorem traceNorm_Hermitian_eq_sum_abs_eigenvalues {A : Matrix n n R} (hA : A.IsHermitian) :
    A.traceNorm = ∑ i, abs (hA.eigenvalues i)

declarations.name: Matrix.traceNorm_nonneg
declarations.doc: The trace norm is nonnegative. Property 9.1.1 in Wilde.
declarations.statement: theorem traceNorm_nonneg (A : Matrix m n R) : 0 ≤ A.traceNorm

declarations.name: Matrix.traceNorm_zero_iff
declarations.doc: The trace norm is zero iff the matrix is zero.
declarations.statement: theorem traceNorm_zero_iff (A : Matrix m n R) : A.traceNorm = 0 ↔ A = 0

declarations.name: Matrix.traceNorm_smul
declarations.doc: The trace norm is homogeneous under scalar multiplication. Property 9.1.2 in Wilde.
declarations.statement: theorem traceNorm_smul (A : Matrix m n R) (c : R) : (c • A).traceNorm = ‖c‖ * A.traceNorm

declarations.name: Matrix.exists_svd_sqrt_eigenvalues
declarations.doc:
Singular value decomposition for square complex matrices, with singular values expressed as
square roots of the eigenvalues of `Aᴴ * A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_svd_sqrt_eigenvalues (A : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    let hH : (Aᴴ * A).IsHermitian := by
      simpa using (Matrix.isHermitian_mul_conjTranspose_self A.conjTranspose)
    ∃ V W : Matrix.unitaryGroup n ℂ,
      A = V.val * Matrix.diagonal (fun i => (Real.sqrt (hH.eigenvalues i) : ℂ)) * W.valᴴ

declarations.name: Matrix.traceNorm_eq_sum_singularValues
declarations.doc: The trace norm of a square complex matrix is the sum of its singular values.
declarations.statement:
theorem traceNorm_eq_sum_singularValues [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    A.traceNorm = ∑ i, singularValues A i

declarations.name: Matrix.traceNorm_eq_sum_singularValuesSorted
declarations.doc: The trace norm of a square complex matrix is the sum of its sorted singular values.
declarations.statement:
theorem traceNorm_eq_sum_singularValuesSorted [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    A.traceNorm = ∑ i : Fin (Fintype.card n), singularValuesSorted A i

declarations.name: Matrix.singularValues_le_opNorm
declarations.doc: Every singular value is bounded by the operator norm.
declarations.statement:
theorem singularValues_le_opNorm [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (i : n) :
    singularValues A i ≤ ‖A‖

declarations.name: Matrix.traceNorm_mul_le_opNorm_traceNorm
declarations.doc: The trace norm is bounded by the operator norm on the left times the trace norm on the right.
declarations.statement:
theorem traceNorm_mul_le_opNorm_traceNorm [DecidableEq n] (A B : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    (A * B).traceNorm ≤ ‖A‖ * B.traceNorm

declarations.name: Matrix.traceNorm_conjTranspose
declarations.doc: The trace norm is invariant under conjugate transpose.
declarations.statement:
theorem traceNorm_conjTranspose (A : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    Aᴴ.traceNorm = A.traceNorm

declarations.name: Matrix.traceNorm_mul_le_traceNorm_opNorm
declarations.doc: The trace norm is bounded by trace norm on the left times operator norm on the right.
declarations.statement:
theorem traceNorm_mul_le_traceNorm_opNorm [DecidableEq n] (A B : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    (A * B).traceNorm ≤ A.traceNorm * ‖B‖

declarations.name: Matrix.traceNorm_sandwich_le
declarations.doc: Multiplication on both sides by contractions does not increase trace norm.
declarations.statement:
theorem traceNorm_sandwich_le [DecidableEq n] {S M T : Matrix n n ℂ} (hS : ‖S‖ ≤ 1)
    (hT : ‖T‖ ≤ 1) : (S * M * T).traceNorm ≤ M.traceNorm

declarations.name: Matrix.abs_trace_le_traceNorm
declarations.doc: The absolute value of the trace is bounded by the trace norm.
declarations.statement:
theorem abs_trace_le_traceNorm (A : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    ‖A.trace‖ ≤ A.traceNorm

declarations.name: Matrix.traceNorm_eq_max_re_tr_U
declarations.doc:
For square complex matrices, the trace norm is the maximum of `re (Tr[U * A])`
over unitaries `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem traceNorm_eq_max_re_tr_U (A : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    IsGreatest {x : ℝ | ∃ U : unitaryGroup n ℂ, Complex.re ((U.val * A).trace) = x} A.traceNorm

declarations.name: Matrix.traceNorm_add_le
declarations.doc: The trace norm satisfies the triangle inequality for square complex matrices.
declarations.statement: theorem traceNorm_add_le (A B : Matrix n n ℂ) : (A + B).traceNorm ≤ A.traceNorm + B.traceNorm

declarations.name: Matrix.PosSemidef.traceNorm_eq_trace
declarations.doc: A positive semidefinite matrix has trace norm equal to its trace.
declarations.statement:
theorem PosSemidef.traceNorm_eq_trace {A : Matrix m m R} (hA : A.PosSemidef) :
    A.traceNorm = A.trace

declarations.name: Matrix.traceNorm_convex
declarations.doc: The trace norm is convex. Property 9.1.5 in Wilde.
declarations.statement:
theorem traceNorm_convex (M N : Matrix n n ℂ) (l : ℝ) (hl : 0 ≤ l ∧ l ≤ 1) :
  ((l:ℂ) • M + ((1 - l) : ℂ) • N).traceNorm ≤ l * M.traceNorm + (1-l) * N.traceNorm

declarations.name: minimax
declarations.doc:
The minimax theorem, at the level of generality we need. For convex, compact, nonempty sets `S`
and `T`in a real topological vector space `M`, and a bilinear function `f` on M, we can exchange
the order of minimizing and maximizing.
declarations.statement:
theorem minimax
  {M : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M] [ContinuousAdd M] [ContinuousSMul ℝ M] [FiniteDimensional ℝ M]
  {N : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup N] [Module ℝ N] [ContinuousAdd N] [ContinuousSMul ℝ N]
  (f : N →L[ℝ] M →L[ℝ] ℝ)
  (S : Set M) (T : Set N) (hS₁ : IsCompact S) (hT₁ : IsCompact T)
  (hS₂ : Convex ℝ S) (hT₂ : Convex ℝ T) (hS₃ : S.Nonempty) (hT₃ : T.Nonempty)
    : ⨅ x : T, ⨆ y : S, f x y = ⨆ y : S, ⨅ x : T, f x y

declarations.name: LinearMap.BilinForm.minimax
declarations.doc: **Von-Neumann's Minimax Theorem**, specialized to bilinear forms.

theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.minimax

  (hS₂ : Convex ℝ S) (hT₂ : Convex ℝ T) (hS₃ : S.Nonempty) (hT₃ : T.Nonempty)
    : ⨅ x : T, ⨆ y : S, f x y = ⨆ y : S, ⨅ x : T, f x y

declarations.name: LinearMap.BilinForm.minimax'
declarations.doc: Convenience form of `LinearMap.BilinForm.minimax` with the order inf/sup arguments supplied to f flipped.
declarations.statement:
theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.minimax'
  {M : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M] [ContinuousAdd M] [ContinuousSMul ℝ M] [FiniteDimensional ℝ M]
  (f : LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ M)
  (S : Set M) (T : Set M) (hS₁ : IsCompact S) (hT₁ : IsCompact T)

sections.text:
Following https://projecteuclid.org/journals/kodai-mathematical-journal/volume-11/issue-1/Elementary-proof-for-Sions-minimax-theorem/10.2996/kmj/1138038812.full, with some corrections. There are two errors in Lemma 2 and the main theorem: an incorrect step that
`(∀ x, a < f x) → (a < ⨅ x, f x)`. This is repaired by taking an extra `exists_between` to get `a < b < ⨅ ...`, concluding that
`(∀ x, b < f x) → (b ≤ ⨅ x, f x)` and so `(a < ⨅ x, f x)`.

declarations.doc:
**Sion's Minimax theorem**. Because of `ciSup` and `ciInf` junk values when f isn't
bounded, we need to assume that it's bounded above and below.
declarations.statement:
theorem sion_minimax
  (h_bddA : BddAbove (Set.image2 f S T))
  (h_bddB : BddBelow (Set.image2 f S T))

modules.title: Tactic for `Commute`
modules.doc:
This tactic uses `aesop` to discharge goals relating to the `Commute` relation. It mostly
tries to do straightforward recursion on expressions, along with some basic normalization
of ring operations.

modules.title: Commutes Rule Set
modules.doc:
This module defines the `Commutes` Aesop rule set which is used by the
`commutes` tactic. Aesop rule sets only become visible once the file in which
they're declared is imported, so we must put this declaration into its own file.

modules.title: Typeclass instances for `ULift`
modules.doc:
This file equips `ULift` with algebraic and analytic typeclass instances lifted from the
underlying type, including `Star`, `StarMul`, `StarRing`, `NormedField`, `DenselyNormedField`
and `RCLike` structures, together with the corresponding `simp` lemmas relating operations on
`ULift.{v, u} α` to operations on the underlying `α`.

declarations.doc:
Conjugating a linear map by a unitary operator gives a map whose μ-eigenspace is
isomorphic (same dimension) as those of the original linear map.
declarations.statement:

    eigenspace T μ ≃ₗ[𝕜] eigenspace (U.val * T * star (U.val)) μ
